Role-based differences are limited under complete ownership but become more evident under separated ownership, particularly for intermediary actors. Beyond these contextual patterns, social influence and perceived network effects emerge as the most stable determinants, while performance expectancy and facilitating conditions play conditional roles, suggesting that perceived platform benefits and support mechanisms increase willingness only when they create clear value, reduce uncertainty, and lower participation burdens. Theoretically, this study advances maritime platform governance research by conceptualizing data ownership as a role-contingent governance arrangement rather than as a uniform determinant of willingness to share data. Practically, the findings provide guidance for designing role-aligned data ownership and incentive structures to support sustainable maritime data collaboration.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Data-driven comparison of airline passenger flight supply using optimal transport theory
Authors: Qian Liu, Paul Rochet, Chantal Roucolle
Abstract: This study develops an optimal transport (OT) framework for measuring pairwise airline supply dissimilarity across heterogeneous route networks. By representing each airline as a distribution of seat capacity or flight frequency across routes and defining route-level transportation costs, the framework provides a flexible and interpretable approach to comparing carriers beyond traditional measures based on multimarket contact or aggregate concentration. To illustrate its versatility, three OT-based dissimilarity indices are introduced to capture differences in seasonal supply positioning, geographic market proximity, and route-length structure. The framework is applied to European scheduled passenger flights for 32 airlines between 2016 and 2025. The empirical results show that airline relationships are multidimensional, with different patterns of similarity emerging across carrier types and network characteristics. A longitudinal analysis relative to the 2016 baseline reveals heterogeneous adjustment trajectories across airlines and indicates post-pandemic convergence in some dimensions of network organization alongside persistent differentiation in others. Overall, the proposed OT framework provides a general tool for inferring airline similarity from transport distances, assessing resilience and recovery following shocks, and examining structural change over time. The framework can also support the construction of airline peer groups for benchmarking, and the medium- to long-term monitoring of structural network recovery following major market shocks.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Global airport connectivity and resilience: a data-driven approach and inverse-U relationship, 1996–2024
Authors: Yilin Zhang, Tommy Cheung, Anming Zhang
Abstract: This study analyzes the long-run evolution of global airport connectivity from 1996 to 2024 and examines how resilience to major shocks varies across the connectivity distribution. Using an extended Global Airport Connectivity Index (GACI) panel covering 101,049 airport–year observations and 5428 airports, it documents steady expansion punctuated by crises, a redistribution of connectivity across continents, and an increasingly multipolar hub hierarchy. The paper then develops a reproducible, multi-crisis resilience index with three components: depth (magnitude of loss), speed (pace of recovery), and adaptability (post-shock upgrading in the global hierarchy). The index aggregates realized airport performance across multiple major shocks, applies empirical-Bayes regularization to improve comparability across airports with uneven shock histories, and filters micro-fluctuations below 1% to reduce noise. Relating resilience to connectivity uncovers a consistent inverse-U relationship: resilience increases with connectivity up to a mid-scale range and declines among the most globally connected hubs. This pattern is consistent with greater exposure to synchronized shocks and scale-related operational frictions, although the analysis identifies the relationship rather than its underlying mechanisms. Robustness checks include alternative component weightings, pre-COVID estimates, crisis-specific recovery horizons, alternative adaptability definitions, region-specific COVID timing, an alternative fixed-scale connectivity construction, and non-overlapping crisis windows. These checks confirm the stability of the pattern. By embedding airport-level recovery behaviour in a three-decade network context, the GACI–resilience framework provides a systematic basis for comparing hub types and benchmarking realized resilience, and for informing route-development, infrastructure-planning, and policy strategies during pandemics, geopolitical disruptions, and other major shocks.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Train scheduling with variable running speeds and multiple train compositions
Authors: Hanchuan Pan, Siqi Guo, Fan Xiao, Wei Liu, Zhe Liang
Abstract: In recent years, frequent small-scale emergencies, such as extreme weather events, have often led to significant passenger flow fluctuations in metro systems. To better accommodate this fluctuated demand, the operators are required to design irregular timetables where both train arrival/departure times at each station and composition modes for each train service vary dynamically. Accordingly, this paper investigates an integrated train scheduling problem that simultaneously addresses (1) the train running speed optimization strategy that seeks to find the best train trajectories for a series of trains, and (2) the multiple train compositions optimization strategy that provides sufficient transport capacity with the least rolling stock units. To this end, we propose a novel nonlinear mixed integer optimization model for minimizing the total costs of energy consumption and service quality for passengers, where the train running speed is innovatively treated as a decision variable. A conic reformulation technique is proposed, such that the nonlinear parts of the developed model can be reformulated as second-order cone constraints, which can be efficiently handled by commercial solvers. Two computational experiments involving a relatively small- and large-sized cases derived from the subway line 17 in Shanghai are tested to assess the quality of our method. The results suggest that this approach can be used by operators to derive a high-quality energy-efficient train timetable.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Truck-drone collaborative routing with flexible cross-truck operations and slot constraints
Authors: Hang Fan, Zhuxi Zhang, Tong Guo, Wenbo Du, Xuechen Gu, Tao Song, Defu Lin
Abstract: Truck-drone collaborative routing faces critical operational bottlenecks in realistic logistics scenarios due to strict return constraints and limited physical recovery slots. We address these challenges by proposing a novel Mixed-Integer Linear Programming model for the Flexible Assignment Vehicle Routing Problem with Drones and Slot Constraints (FA-VRPDSC). By decoupling drones from specific launch vehicles, the model enables flexible cross-truck operations and dynamic task assignments across the entire fleet under strict slot capacity limits. To efficiently solve this complex combinatorial problem, we develop a tailored Memetic Algorithm with Adaptive Large Neighborhood Perturbation (MA-ALNP). The algorithm leverages a dual-chain representation to jointly encode routing sequences and collaboration states. To navigate the tightly coupled temporal and spatial constraints, we integrate specialized repair operators and an adaptive destroy-and-repair shaking mechanism that effectively prevents premature convergence. Computational results confirm the algorithm’s exact optimality on small instances and its structural superiority on large-scale benchmarks, significantly outperforming advanced heuristics in minimizing total makespan. Our sensitivity analysis ultimately highlights that extended drone endurance is pivotal for activating flexible cross-truck docking and maximizing fleet coordination.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Experimental study on low-carbon supply chain management using symbolic award
Authors: Junjun Liu, Lifang Gao, Ning Li
Abstract: Symbolic awards, such as low-carbon supplier certification, actively motivate suppliers to strengthen their carbon reduction initiatives and advance sustainable supply chain management. Yet, when low-carbon suppliers remain scarce, these awards intensify buyer competition and raise the costs of maintaining supplier relationships. Notably, several suppliers leverage awards to build reputations that improve their bargaining power, creating strategic dilemmas around public disclosure. This study develops a two-stage game model and tests its predictions through controlled experiments to examine how alternative award formats influence supplier and buyer outcomes. Our results show that a symbolic award significantly encourages suppliers to reduce emissions and improve buyers’ bottom lines. However, award format shapes buyer utility in critical ways: public awards compel buyers to invest more in retaining suppliers, while private awards deliver greater financial value to buyers. In markets with few low-carbon suppliers, buyers often need to allocate more resources to relationship management, while suppliers may resist private incentives if they perceive reputational drawbacks. These findings highlight the need for carefully designed disclosure strategies to balance costs and benefits for both sides, thereby fostering more effective and sustainable supply chains.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Modeling and solving the two-echelon open vehicle routing problem with autonomous delivery vehicles
Authors: Wenhui Bai, Peng Liu, Tianyu Wang, Wenchao Wei
Abstract: With the rapid advancement of driving automation technology, the logistics industry is increasingly adopting autonomous delivery vehicles (ADVs), particularly within hybrid logistics modes. This study investigates a novel delivery system that integrates traditional trucks and ADVs within a two-echelon distribution framework, formalized as the two-echelon open vehicle routing problem with autonomous delivery vehicles (2E-OVRP-ADVs). A defining characteristic of this system is that ADVs can depart from one satellite and return to another, an open-route structure that reduces empty deadhead trips but creates vehicle flow among satellites. The core novelty of this work is the joint consideration of open routes and vehicle imbalance management. We introduce the concept of tolerance for imbalance (TI), which explicitly bounds the post-delivery number of ADVs at each satellite, thereby constraining the vehicle redistribution induced by the open-route mechanism. The problem is first modeled as a mixed-integer linear program using an arc-based formulation. To improve computational efficiency, a path-based reformulation is solved via a branch-and-price algorithm. An adaptive large neighborhood search metaheuristic is used to generate initial solution pools and assist in the pricing subproblem before invoking the exact pricing procedure. For the exact pricing, both a commodity-flow formulation and a Dantzig-Fulkerson-Johnson formulation with a lazy-cut separation procedure are solved concurrently, with the one yielding the smaller optimality gap adopted. Extensive numerical experiments validate the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed algorithm and provide managerial insights into how open routes and TI impact total routing costs, offering valuable guidance for optimizing ADV-enabled logistics systems.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Energy-aware drone-based parcel delivery problem with multi-charging mode availability
Authors: Yanfang Ma, Mengdi Yuan, Zhinan Wu, Rui Qiu, Feng Li
Abstract: As drone delivery moves toward practical logistics operations, smart parcel lockers can be extended from parcel storage facilities to drone-supporting infrastructure with multi-charging mode capabilities. However, charging modes differ in charging speed and operational cost, and charging-mode availability varies among smart parcel lockers in practice. To minimize the total cost, this paper proposes an energy-aware drone-based parcel delivery problem with multi-charging mode availability (EDPDP-MCMA). For realism, we develop a comprehensive nonlinear drone energy consumption function related to payload, the entire flight process, wind, and pitch angle. Furthermore, we formulate the EDPDP-MCMA as a mixed-integer nonlinear programming model (MINLP) and reformulate it as a mixed-integer linear programming model through the discretization of the payload values. To address large-scale problems, an improved local-adaptive large neighborhood search (ILALNS) algorithm is designed. Numerical experiments are conducted to evaluate the computational performance of the ILALNS, and to analyze the effects of charging-mode availability, energy consumption function, and wind conditions on the total cost. In addition, a real-world case study in Hangzhou, China, is conducted to demonstrate the practical applicability of multi-charging mode availability. The results indicate that the proposed model and algorithm can effectively support drone routing and provide insights into charging-mode availability for smart locker-based drone delivery systems.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Population-weighted transport pressure and its inequality causally shape global socioeconomic development
Authors: Xianmin Ye, Chenyang Shuai, Xi Chen, Bu Zhao
Abstract: Rapid urbanisation, population growth and continued economic expansion have placed many national systems under rising supply pressure. However, how transport infrastructure supply pressure and its inequality within countries relate to socioeconomic development outcomes remains unclear. Here we develop two globally comparable indices, a Transport Infrastructure Supply Pressure index (TISP) and a Transport Infrastructure Supply Pressure Inequality index (TISPI), to quantify population-weighted supply pressure and its internal inequality for 180 countries in 2020 and to examine their associations with key socioeconomic indicators. On average, TISP in the Global South is about 3.5 times that in the Global North, while TISPI is about 1.4 times higher. Moreover, TISP and TISPI are closely linked to socioeconomic outcomes, with higher TISP associated with a lower economic development level and higher TISPI associated with greater income inequality and faster urbanisation, and these relationships exhibit directional evidences. These findings underscore the necessity of optimising transport infrastructure allocation to relieve supply pressure and improve supply–demand matching, thereby guiding transport investment towards more inclusive and sustainable growth.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Deep reinforcement learning for optimizing mobile depots allocation and hybrid order dispatch in last-mile delivery under multi-participants behavioral uncertainty
Authors: Shixuan Hou, Chengming Hu, Annabathuni Sandeep Chowdary, Bissan Ghaddar, Joe Naoum-Sawaya, Jie Gao
Abstract: As last-mile delivery demand continues to grow and customer preferences become increasingly diverse, traditional single-mode logistics systems are inadequate in addressing the complexity and variability of modern urban delivery environments. In this paper, we propose an innovative hybrid last-mile delivery system that leverages mobile depots as intermediate hubs, integrating crowd-shipping, and customer self-pickup, to enhance cost-effectiveness. However multiple stakeholders in the system have conflicting interests, ignoring their behavioral uncertainties can impair operational efficiency and increase delivery costs. For example, customers and crowd-shippers may compete for the limited storage capacity of mobile depots, and crowd-shippers may be unwilling to deliver orders that customers decline to pick up. Specifically, the study captures crowd-shippers’ order-acceptance behavior and customers’ self-pickup choice through two binomial logit models, and embeds these behavioral components into a stochastic mixed-integer programming model. This model jointly optimizes mobile depots allocation and order dispatch decisions, aiming to minimize the expected total operational cost. Considering computational complexity of this model, we propose PRiME-DQN, a reinforcement learning framework that incorporates behavior-prioritized resource filtering, action biasing, and model-efficient temperature tuning to accelerate convergence and improve solution quality. A case study on Amazon’s last-mile delivery in Seattle shows that the proposed hybrid model achieves up to 49.5% cost reduction in low-shipper settings and 11.3% in higher-shipper settings compared to a crowd-shipping system, while also consistently surpassing the self-pickup baseline by 3–6%. Extensive scaling experiments show that PRiME-DQN produces high-quality feasible solutions efficiently. For the largest instances, it achieves delivery costs 1.97% lower than Gurobi’s best incumbent solution obtained within the 3,600-second time limit, while reducing the solution time to approximately 1400 seconds.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Customized first-and-last-mile ridesharing services with electric modular autonomous vehicles
Authors: Bo Sun, Qiang Meng
Abstract: This study proposes an interesting and viable first-and-last-mile ridesharing service (FLMRS) that leverages electric modular autonomous vehicles (EMAVs) to enhance public transportation (PT) accessibility. A platoon advantage of assembled EMAVs to form a fully connected EMAV (CEMAV) can reduce the operational cost and simultaneously satisfy customized ridesharing needs. Specifically, passengers can select whether to accept ridesharing with others, which are assigned to adaptable EMAVs within a CEMAV. Given the electric nature of a CEMAV fleet, we formulate the FLMRS problem as a set-covering model that accounts for time-dependent energy consumption, partial charging operations, nonlinear charging functions, restricted charging times, and capacitated public charging infrastructures. To consider the unknown availability of limited public chargers, we propose a predict-then-optimize approach that first forecasts charger availability using both endogenous and exogenous features and converts the prediction results into uncertainty-adjusted charger capacities before optimization. We then incorporate the charger capacities as input parameters to tackle the FLMRS by optimization methods. A data-driven column generation (DDCG) method within a rolling-horizon framework is developed to solve the real-time optimization problem with dynamic request arrivals. To enhance computational efficiency in solving the pricing subproblems of DDCG, we utilize two advanced acceleration techniques to reduce label exploration. Extensive computational experiments using real-world data from Singapore validate the effectiveness of the proposed methods in obtaining high-quality solutions. The experimental results demonstrate the advantages of the predict-then-optimize framework in improving capacity utilization and matching personalized travel needs with suitable CEMAV configurations.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: A dual-phase spatio-temporal deep reinforcement learning approach for the time-dependent green multi-depot vehicle routing problem with time windows
Authors: Yang Zou, Xiaokun Huang, Yunqiang Yin, T.C.E. Cheng
Abstract: In time-varying traffic conditions, departure timing affects travel duration, arrival schedules, and environmental performance, making temporal decisions an important component of green multi-depot vehicle routing. This study investigates the Time-Dependent Green Multi-Depot Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows. It incorporates proactive node-level waiting into spatial route planning, whereas conventional immediate-departure approaches treat temporal scheduling as an implicit consequence of the selected route. We propose a Dual-Phase Spatio-Temporal Policy (DPSTP) framework based on deep reinforcement learning. The framework adopts a route-first, schedule-second decision paradigm, where spatial route construction and route-conditioned departure scheduling are sequentially determined and jointly optimized to minimize a total cost comprising operational duration, emission-proxy costs, and lateness penalties. Computational experiments on synthetic benchmark instances (n=100) show that DPSTP achieves the lowest mean total cost among the compared methods; Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search, POMO, and the OR-Tools solver incur 22.38%, 12.66%, and 8.79% higher total cost, respectively. A case study on a large-scale Cordeau instance further shows that proactive waiting with an expanded temporal action space (a relaxed-window reference scenario) reduces the emission-proxy cost by 10.4% and total cost by 18.1% relative to immediate departure, with a moderate increase in lateness penalties, while the default bounded policy reduces total cost by 14.0%. These results provide empirical evidence that route-conditioned temporal scheduling can improve objective performance under the time-varying traffic conditions and benchmark settings considered in this study.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: A full-sample longitudinal trajectory reconstruction framework for signalized intersection approach lanes in a vehicle-infrastructure cooperation environment
Authors: Tingting Ren, Chengxin Fu, Yangsheng Jiang, Zhihong Yao, Yunxia Wu, Kefan Chen
Abstract: Vehicle trajectories contain abundant spatial–temporal information that can be utilized for traffic state estimation and parameter optimization. In the vehicle-infrastructure cooperation environment, connected automated vehicles (CAVs) can provide their trajectory data and perceive the trajectory data of nearby vehicles within a specific range. Moreover, these trajectory data can be shared and cross-validated with fixed detectors, offering a novel solution for reconstructing full-sample vehicle trajectories at the signalized intersection. Based on the car-following (CF) model, this paper proposes a trajectory reconstruction framework that integrates CAVs sensing data and camera detection data. This framework can solve the trajectory reconstruction problem for regular vehicles (RVs) between any two consecutive CAVs on the lane. It comprises four key modules: the trajectory reconstruction model (TRM) based on the trailing CAV (TTRM), the TRM based on the leading CAV (LTRM), the Modified LTRM, and the fusion algorithm (FA). Furthermore, NGSIM and simulation data are utilized to validate and analyze the performance of the proposed framework under various CAV penetration rates (PRs) and traffic demands. Results indicate that: (1) compared to the state-of-the-art CF-based algorithms, the proposed framework significantly reduces in terms of position error, queuing position error, moving position error, time error, speed error, and acceleration error with average RMSE reductions of 83.45%, 20.97%, 90.87%, 85.54%, 30.39%, and 28.64% in NGSIM data, respectively, and even more substantial decrease in simulation data. (2) The framework maintains acceptable error rates across different PRs of CAVs and varying traffic volumes. (3) The framework is robust for different CF model parameters in simulation data. The findings can support signalized intersection management and control in the vehicle-infrastructure cooperation environment.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Two-stage distributionally robust optimization for the online retail inventory placement problem
Authors: Zhenhao Deng, Feng Li, Xianyan Yang, Xinyue Jia
Abstract: The rapid growth of online retail has transformed supply chain management, notably through fulfillment flexibility, which allows demand from different customer regions to be served by multiple fulfillment centers. To leverage this flexibility, online retailers allocate inventory for a large number of items across shared fulfillment centers while balancing fixed inventory-placement costs and transportation costs. However, because inventory placement requires advance planning, relying on deterministic demand estimates may lead to severe inventory misallocation and stockouts. Motivated by this, we study a two-stage online retail inventory placement problem under demand uncertainty. In our model, item-level inventory placement decisions are made before actual demand is observed. After demand is realized, transportation decisions are made to split demand fulfillment across multiple fulfillment centers, while shortage costs are incurred when inventory is insufficient. This problem is formulated as a two-stage distributionally robust optimization model over a moment-based ambiguity set. By applying duality theory and enumerating extreme-point scenarios for the continuous random variables, the infinite-dimensional min-max-min formulation is transformed into an equivalent mixed-integer linear program (MILP). An exact algorithm based on the column-and-constraint generation (C&CG) framework is proposed to solve the MILP reformulation. It incorporates problem-specific valid inequalities that provide explicit bounds on the dual variables, thereby tightening the master problem relaxation and improving convergence. To further accelerate convergence, an improved exact algorithm is developed by incorporating a tailored column generation (CG) procedure that identifies multiple scenarios at each iteration. Computational results demonstrate the efficiency of both proposed algorithms and the improved robustness of the distributionally robust model over traditional stochastic programming approaches.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: How construal level can shape buyer responses to supplier labor violations
Authors: Dayna Simpson, Tim Kraft, Marie Segrave
Abstract: Despite widespread organizational commitments to eliminate labor exploitation in supply chains, a substantial gap persists between stated policies and suppliers’ actual practices. Major companies pledge zero tolerance for labor violations at suppliers, yet evidence that buyers follow through with meaningful corrective action when suppliers commit labor violations has been limited. This gap between commitment and enforcement of labor policies by buyers reduces supplier compliance and undermines efforts to improve working conditions in global supply chains. We address the problem of buyer follow-through by exploring whether construal can influence buyers’ responses to supplier labor violations. Construal level is an established driver of managerial behavior in many domains, yet exploration of its role in supply chain decision-making is limited. Using three experiments we show that reducing construal can improve the relationship between buyer responsibility for its suppliers’ workers and buyer willingness to suspend the supplier for a major labor violation. Our findings contribute novel insights for more effective governance of working conditions in supply chains, by: i. identifying that construal can influence buyer willingness to respond to supplier labor violations; and ii. identifying interventions that influence construal and elicit more effective buyer action, including faster reporting, clear labor policies, concrete thinking, and increased expertise. Our research emphasizes the important role of construal in supply chain decision making and its links to managerial understanding of working conditions in supply chains. Our findings advance efforts to encourage more effective action from buyers when labor violations are reported in their supply chain.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Experience-driven value creation in digital airline self-service systems: evidence from a low-cost carrier context
Authors: Maryam Kefi Ben Chehida, Mathieu Dunes, Mourad Chouki, Marina Dabić, Tilo Halaszovich
Abstract: This study examines an experience-driven value creation mechanism in digital airline self-service systems in the low-cost carrier (LCC) context. It focuses on a setting less frequently studied in customer experience research: digitally mediated, low-contact airline services in which booking, check-in, and boarding interfaces function as customer touchpoints embedded in standardized passenger-service processes. From a passenger logistics perspective, these interfaces are part of standardized passenger-service systems through which customers complete sequenced service tasks with limited employee contact. Drawing on means-end theory and service-dominant logic, the study models customer experience (CX) as an antecedent of customer-perceived value (CPV) and behavioral intentions (BIs). Survey data were collected from 330 passengers of a European LCC operating in France and were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM). The analysis reports positive and statistically significant CX → CPV and CPV → BIs effects. The main empirical evidence concerns the indirect CX → CPV → BIs path, whereas the direct CX → BIs path is small in magnitude. In the final model, the CPV composite comprises utilitarian value/control and emotional value. No statistically significant generational cohort moderation is detected in this sample, and robustness checks indicate that the mediated CX → CPV → BIs path remains positive and statistically significant when value-for-money perceptions and travel frequency are considered. The study applies CX theory to low-contact airline environments and examines digital self-service interfaces as passenger touchpoints within standardized LCC service processes. For managers, the results underscore the importance of CX in digitally mediated LCC journeys and direct attention to interface clarity and low-friction task completion.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Generative AI and Machine learning collaboration for container dwell time prediction via data standardization
Authors: Minseop Kim, Takhyeong Kim, Taekhyun Park, Hanbyeol Park, Hyerim Bae
Abstract: Import container dwell time (ICDT) prediction is a key task for improving productivity in container terminals, as accurate predictions enable the reduction of container re-handling operations by yard cranes. Achieving this objective requires accurately predicting the dwell time of individual containers. However, the primary determinants of dwell time-owner information and cargo information-are recorded as unstructured text, which limits their effective use in machine learning models. This study addresses this limitation by proposing a collaborative framework that integrates generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) with machine learning. The proposed framework employs Gen AI to standardize unstructured information into standard international codes, with dynamic re-prediction triggered by electronic data interchange state updates, enabling the machine learning model to predict ICDT accurately. Extensive experiments conducted on real container terminal data demonstrate that the proposed methodology achieves a 13.88% improvement in mean absolute error compared to conventional models that do not utilize standardized information. Furthermore, applying the improved predictions to container stacking strategies achieves up to 14.68% reduction in the number of relocations, thereby empirically validating the potential of Gen AI to enhance productivity in container terminal operations. Overall, this study provides both technical and methodological insights into the adoption of Gen AI in port logistics and its effectiveness.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: An equity-constrained two-stage distributionally robust optimization model for urban disaster preparation
Authors: Xihui Wang, Zikai Chen, Yu Fan
Abstract: Natural disasters are becoming more frequent and complex and are characterized by greater uncertainty. Urban areas are especially vulnerable because high population density and concentrated infrastructure can amplify disaster impacts. Two-stage distributionally robust optimization is a widely adopted method to deal with the uncertainty in disaster logistics problems. However, most existing studies lack precise demand assessment and general equity concerns. To fill the research gap, we first propose a more precise demand assessment method with the consideration of urban environmental information (e.g., fine-grained urban building features), and then incorporate an explicit equity constraint into the second-stage resource allocation. Through applying affine decision rules and copositive programming reformulations, we solve this complex random recourse problem by deriving a computationally tractable approximation. With a numerical experiment based on real-world data in Hefei, China, we find that our approach outperforms the deterministic model and sample average approximation model in both average cost and robustness. Compared to the model without equity consideration, our solution narrows community satisfaction rates gaps with a marginal cost increase and enhances urban resilience by increasing pre-positioned inventory. This work provides a decision-making tool for achieving equitable and resilient urban disaster logistics.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Robust trajectory optimization for communication-constrained drone logistics under wind and payload uncertainty
Authors: Xia Zhou, Jianpeng Ding, Yuanbo Li
Abstract: The rapid expansion of drone delivery services has created an urgent need for planning tools that can guarantee mission feasibility under physical uncertainties and strict communication constraints. However, existing approaches treat these factors in isolation or rely on deterministic assumptions that fail at deployment, leaving a critical gap between nominal planning and operational reliability. Motivated by this gap, we propose a unified robust optimization framework for multi-drone pickup and delivery systems that simultaneously addresses wind disturbances, payload variability, and strict communication rate requirements. Our model integrates aerodynamic power consumption, Shannon-capacity constraints, leg-based budgeted wind uncertainty sets, and polyhedral payload uncertainty sets into a single mixed-integer second-order cone program (MISOCP). Theoretically, we prove that the robust flight speed constraint admits an exact SOCP representation and derive exact linear duals for the payload constraints via strong duality. Because spatial coupling constraints invalidate traditional decomposition approaches, we design a multi-start hybrid (MSH) algorithm. This algorithm employs a stochastic master problem with Log-normal perturbations to generate diverse routing skeletons and a continuous SOCP subproblem for rigorous physical feasibility verification, coupled with a bottleneck-directed local search. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate substantial performance improvements over existing methods. Compared to exact solvers, the MSH algorithm significantly reduces computation time while maintaining near-optimal solution quality. Crucially, for large-scale instances where exact solvers completely fail, it remains a non-trivial method capable of producing feasible solutions. These results confirm that the framework bridges the tractability gap between exact optimization and heuristic dispatch, establishing it as a highly practical tool for real-world drone fleet deployment.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: A dual-channel model integrating wavelet denoising and multi-head self-attention mechanism for predicting train travel times of China-Europe railway express
Authors: Yongxiang Zhang, Liting Gu, Jingwei Guo, Xin Hu, Xu Yan, Zhen-Song Chen
Abstract: The China-Europe Railway Express (CRE) is an important logistics corridor linking China and Europe. However, due to various influencing factors during transportation, existing prediction models generally fail to correctly represent the complex nonlinear spatio-temporal aspects of the CRE train travel times, leading to incorrect train travel time predictions. To overcome this challenge, this study proposes a Multi-scale Wavelet Denoising (MWD)-Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) dual-channel model incorporating a Multi-head Self-attention Mechanism (MHSA) (MWD-CNN-GRU-MHSA) to forecast CRE train travel times. The MWD is first employed to extract features and reduce the noise in the historical train travel times, aiming to improve data quality. Then, a dual-channel model combining CNN and GRU is established, where the CNN learns local spatial patterns and the GRU handles time-dependent features, processing the input time series in parallel. MHSA is introduced into the dual-channel model to flexibly allocate weights on salient fused features derived from the two branches. A series of comparative experiments are conducted to evaluate the proposed method based on real-world CRE round-trip train travel time data. The experimental findings show that the MWD-CNN-GRU-MHSA framework outperforms thirteen mainstream baseline models in forecasting performance and generalization. Specifically, the MWD-CNN-GRU-MHSA model exhibits robust performance in CRE train travel time estimation, with root mean square error (RMSE) of 7.516 hours, mean absolute error (MAE) of 5.053 hours, mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 1.259%, and coefficient of determination ( R 2) of 0.907. In conclusion, the MWD-CNN-GRU-MHSA model demonstrates strong stability and robustness, with good adaptability to complex transportation data. It offers reliable technical support for rail dispatching optimization and CRE service quality improvement.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Truck-drone routing problem under time-dependent traffic congestion: A novel variable neighborhood search metaheuristic
Authors: Shaorui Zhou, Xiaorui Liu, Jihong Chen, Lingxiao Wu, Zhou Xu, Min Zhao
Abstract: Urban last-mile delivery faces growing demand, stricter delivery-duration requirements, and persistent road congestion. Truck-drone coordination offers a promising response, but most existing studies simplify either truck travel conditions or drone endurance by assuming constant truck speeds or fixed drone flight capability. This paper studies a truck-drone routing problem with time-dependent traffic congestion and load-dependent drone endurance, termed TDC-LDE-TDRP. We formulate a mixed-integer linear programming model that jointly optimizes truck routes, drone flights, customer assignment, and service timing, while capturing time-dependent truck travel and nonlinear payload-dependent drone energy consumption. To solve large-scale instances, we develop PRS-VNS, a novel variable neighborhood search metaheuristic that integrates parallel exploration, structured restart, and decomposition-based re-optimization to improve search stability and solution quality. Computational experiments show that PRS-VNS outperforms benchmark heuristics in solution quality, robustness, and convergence behavior. Using real customer locations and road congestion data from Shenzhen, China, we further show that truck-drone coordination is economically viable and can mitigate the cost impact of congestion. The results also reveal that the marginal value of drones depends jointly on delivery duration and congestion intensity, that jointly modeling TDC and LDE produces a positive complementary effect, and that improved drone endurance may alter the coordinated delivery structure.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Credit-driven quality coordination in cross-regional fresh-food supply chains: A tripartite dynamic game and policy optimization
Authors: Chao Zhao, Yongmei Chi, Nini Gao, Shunshu Bao
Abstract: Cross-regional fresh-food supply chains expand market access, but they also make quality governance more challenging as product deterioration, transportation delays, information asymmetry, and fragmented regulation interact over time. This study examines how credit supervision can be integrated with supply-chain contracts and public policy to coordinate quality investment, logistics timeliness, and fiscal sustainability. We develop a tripartite differential game model involving a manufacturer, a retailer, and a government regulator, in which product quality, corporate credit, and policy instruments co-evolve as state variables. The Markov perfect equilibrium is approximated using relaxed best-response iteration with GPOPS-II. The numerical results yield four insights into supply-chain governance. First, under baseline calibration, the effective decision cycle is approximately 11 days; longer planning horizons sharply reduce profits and welfare because logistics and quality-adjustment frictions accumulate over time. Second, quality improvement and credit accumulation reinforce each other, but credit ratings respond with a lag, making early operational decisions particularly important. Third, subsidies and penalties are effective only within appropriate ranges: weak penalties fail to deter firms’ low-quality behavior, whereas excessive subsidy effectiveness crowds out firms’ own quality-improvement and freshness-preservation efforts. Fourth, upstream quality improvement generates downstream spillovers through demand and logistics-cost channels, making government welfare more sensitive to source-side quality efficiency than to several downstream policy parameters. These findings suggest that regulators should adopt strong early intervention with gradual withdrawal, while firms should align quality-improvement investment, freshness-preservation effort, and transportation-cycle decisions within the perishability window of fresh-food logistics.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Low-altitude delivery path planning for unmanned aerial vehicles based on optimal energy consumption
Authors: Xiaowen Sha, Shuang Qiu, Zhihao Xu
Abstract: In low-altitude logistics, Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) energy consumption exhibits strong nonlinear characteristics due to complex micro-meteorology and dynamic payloads. Traditional geometric routing algorithms struggle to maximize true endurance. This paper proposes a global energy-optimal path planning framework for micro-meteorological environments. First, an AttnHeadLSTM network integrating physical coupled features and temporal attention is constructed to capture the high-dimensional hysteresis effects of energy consumption. Second, a steady-state sequence replication mechanism and a spatial cost tensor map are introduced to seamlessly embed the deep kinematic model into a heading-aware A* search. Under predefined wind field scenarios and payload loads, experimental results verify the framework’s capability to autonomously formulate scenario-adaptive optimization tactics, opting for wind-assisted detours when unloaded and straight trajectories at maximum payload. The approach achieves up to 41.05 % energy savings, offering an effective energy optimization method for mission planning in low-altitude logistics UAVs. Open-source link: https://github.com/Shaxiaowen/UAV-Path-Planning .
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Synchromodal bi-objective two-stage stochastic optimization for container and power unit allocation
Authors: Milton Caballero, Andrés D. González
Abstract: Container repositioning and power-unit deployment are typically planned in isolation, despite being operationally coupled in practice. Moreover, these processes are continually affected by diverse uncertainties-such as fluctuating demand and variable availability of containers and other resources-which further increases the complexity of planning and operations. To address these challenges, we propose an integrated Bi-Objective Two-Stage Stochastic Mixed-Integer model for the landside component of intermodal container logistics. The model jointly allocates containers across the drayage network and power units across the trucking network under demand uncertainty. In the first stage, the model determines repositioning, leasing, and initial deployment, utilizing leasing decisions as the structural link between the two networks. In the second stage, once scenarios are realized, both networks execute recourse flows. We employ the ε-constraint method to trace the Pareto-efficient frontiers, revealing that, for the modeled instances, sequential “siloed” strategies are mathematically dominated solutions. A numerical study based on the Florida intermodal network exposes a critical economic asymmetry in the value of coordination. We identify a “strategic efficiency zone” where the trucking sector can realize significant cost savings (' 40%) while imposing negligible penalties (' 0.5%) on the drayage sector. This finding challenges the assumption that supply chain integration is a zero-sum game, suggesting that, in this setting, a key barrier to coordination may be not economic incompatibility but the absence of structural mechanisms to align independent objective functions. The results quantify the opportunity cost of decentralized coordination, suggesting that a cooperative mechanism-enabled by minor adjustments to leasing locations-can yield notable systemic value without requiring significant financial concessions from the primary stakeholder.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Two-stage optimization framework for electric vehicle automatic charging stations with differential charging strategies in photovoltaic-energy storage system microgrid
Authors: Jing Liu, Zhou Zhang, Mingyang Pei, Lingshu Zhong, Kun Gao
Abstract: The rapid expansion of the electric vehicle (EV) market has intensified the demand for efficient charging infrastructure, yet conventional fixed-charger paradigms suffer from low utilization rates, pronounced grid peak-valley disparities, and insufficient renewable energy absorption due to the one-vehicle-one-charger binding constraint. This study proposes a two-stage robust optimization framework for Electric Vehicle Automatic Charging Stations integrated with a photovoltaic-energy storage system microgrid: Stage 1 employs a reinforcement-learning-enhanced NSGA-II and TOPSIS to simultaneously optimize economic efficiency, reclassification count, and grid load variance under a budget-of-uncertainty formulation that jointly handles EV arrival/departure time uncertainty and photovoltaic output variability; Stage 2 combines CPLEX-based exact EV grouping with a Wolpertinger-DDPG architecture for dynamic rail-mounted mobile charger (RMC) assignment, enabling a one-charger-serves-multiple-vehicles paradigm through rail-mounted robotic charging arms. A scheduling-flexibility-based EV trichotomy with a formal reclassification safety-net mechanism and a price-inversion-preventing compensation design are embedded to guarantee differentiated yet equitable charging services. Comprehensive validation was conducted across three urban scenarios with 10,000 users. These results confirm that the proposed framework offers a scalable and robust solution for large-scale sustainable EV charging infrastructure deployment.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Engineering a win-win: Optimal group buying strategies for food delivery platforms and merchants
Authors: Han Fang, Jinshu Cai, Sisi Jian
Abstract: With the rapid growth of e-commerce, group buying (GB) has become an effective promotional strategy for on-demand food delivery platforms such as Uber Eats and Meituan (e.g., Meituan’s Pin Hao Fan). In this setting, platforms may introduce GB programs that allow consumers to obtain price discounts by waiting for order consolidation and engaging in self-collection. This study examines whether and how GB can create value for platforms and merchants while accounting for consumers’ price-time trade-offs. We develop an integrated analytical framework that combines consumer choice modeling, continuous-approximation-based delivery cost analysis, and a Stackelberg game to characterize the equilibrium interactions among the platform, the merchant, and consumers. The platform determines a subsidy rate to share the merchant’s discount cost, while the merchant optimizes the GB discount level and group size in response to consumer participation decisions that balance price savings against waiting inconvenience. Our analysis identifies GB as a market-expansion mechanism that stimulates demand by converting existing consumers to GB orders and attracting price-sensitive consumers who would otherwise not order. When GB events are launched, merchants can optimize their discount and group-size decisions to achieve higher profits than under the no-GB benchmark, whereas the platform benefits from launching GB only under specific market conditions. We also find that the platform’s profit-maximizing policy may diverge from the social optimum, resulting in lower merchant subsidies and reduced consumer surplus. Beyond theoretical insights, this study highlights managerial implications by showing how merchants can leverage GB under different market conditions and how platforms can adjust their policies to balance profit maximization with broader social welfare.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Electric truck–drone routing problem with flight-sensitive zones and partial truck recharging: A multi-objective optimization framework
Authors: Negar Jahanbakhsh Javid, Sharan Srinivas
Abstract: Efficient and sustainable last-mile logistics has become increasingly important as delivery networks expand amid rising environmental regulations and evolving airspace safety requirements. Collaborative electric truck–drone systems offer a promising alternative to conventional delivery but introduce new planning challenges when drones traverse flight-sensitive zones (FSZs). These zones are legally accessible airspaces where connectivity may weaken or additional monitoring is required (e.g., congested urban corridors, areas near hospitals or schools, or regions with high-rise buildings), resulting in measurable exposure rather than unsafe flight conditions. Despite extensive research on truck–drone coordination, existing studies typically assume unrestricted airspace and overlook the trade-offs that emerge when exposure within FSZs must be managed alongside delivery efficiency. This study introduces the Multi-Objective Electric Vehicle Routing Problem with Drones and Flight-Sensitive Zones (MO-EVRPD-FSZ), which integrates synchronized truck–drone operations while accounting for partial recharging of electric trucks. A mixed integer linear programming model (MILP) is proposed to balance delivery completion time and cumulative drone exposure to FSZs. The formulation is further strengthened with valid inequalities and lower bounds to improve computational tractability. To solve large-scale instances, a Multi-Objective Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (MOALNS) and its restart-enhanced variant (MOALNS-RP) are developed and benchmarked against Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II). Computational experiments show that MOALNS-RP approximates the exact ε-constraint solutions with over a 99% reduction in CPU time on small instances and yields stronger Pareto-front coverage and solution-set density than NSGA-II on the large-instance benchmark set. Sensitivity analyses show that fleet size, drone endurance, and truck energy use jointly shape the efficiency–exposure trade-off. The results provide planning insights for fleet configuration and risk-aware operation of hybrid truck–drone systems.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Pricing and frequency decisions in RoRo-road freight competition: A multi-leader game-theoretic model
Authors: Michell Queiroz, Dario Pacino, Seyed Parsa Parvasi
Abstract: This paper proposes a game-theoretic framework to study competitive interactions between road transport and Short Sea Shipping in Roll-on/Roll-off (RoRo) cargo services. We model the interaction as a multi-leader-common-follower game, where sea and road operators set prices, and the sea operator also adjusts service frequency. Shippers respond using a logit-based choice model where utility depends on price and transit time. We compute the solution through an iterative best-response procedure that converges to a Nash equilibrium among leaders within a Stackelberg hierarchy between leaders and followers. Computational experiments on three European corridors (Gothenburg-Ghent, Cuxhaven-Immingham, and Rosslare-Dunkirk) explore scenarios with varying cost structures and customer sensitivities. Results show that sea transport generally gains market share, but profitability is notably stronger when price sensitivity is low. When price sensitivity is high, operators face challenges unless frequency increases are applied strategically, particularly in settings with high time sensitivity, since higher frequency reduces waiting times and attracts sufficient additional demand to maintain competitiveness. We introduce a frequency-viability index, which signals when an additional weekly sailing is economically justified. These findings highlight the strategic role of pricing and frequency in promoting modal shift and suggest that policy support may be necessary for long-term competitiveness.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Airline planning under market uncertainty and passengers’ choice: Data-driven distributionally robust decomposition-based optimization framework
Authors: Ali Papi-RAD, Mir Saman Pishvaee, Hadi Sahebi
Abstract: A pivotal challenge in the Airline Tactical Flight Schedule Planning (ATFSP) is to construct an integrated and data-driven solution framework for jointly optimizing flight frequency, timetable development, and fleet assignment that maximizes revenue while ensuring robustness under market volatility. This paper first formally describes and formulates the ATFSP problem, incorporating passengers’ choice behavior and Origin-Destination (O-D) demand uncertainty. We then propose a data-driven Distributionally Robust Optimization (DRO) model that explicitly captures market uncertainty and passenger choice effects, enabling endogenous recapture of spilled demand. To incorporate discrete choice behavior, we develop an Augmented/Adjustable Multinomial Logit (AMNL) model together with an exact linear reformulation that enhances computational tractability. To address inherent O-D market uncertainty, we introduce a novel machine learning (ML)-assisted approach to construct a discrepancy-based distributional ambiguity set, which forms the core of the proposed DRO framework. Furthermore, to efficiently solve the proposed DRO model, we employ a decomposition-based approach leveraging a Column-and-Constraint Generation (C&CG) scheme with a newly designed distribution-generation subproblem. Computational experiments, including a domestic route network case and various randomly simulated instances, validate the robustness and efficiency of the proposed solution framework. The results confirm its ability to guarantee robustness, passenger-centricity, and computational tractability, which are essential features for contemporary airline planning. Moreover, comparative analyses conclusively demonstrate: (i) the superior robustness of the proposed ML-enriched discrete l 1 -ball DRO approach over traditional uncertainty modeling paradigms; (ii) the computational efficiency of the tailored C&CG algorithm compared to off-the-shelf solvers; and (iii) the substantial benefits achieved by incorporating passengers’ choice via the AMNL model over conventional solutions.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: A logic-based Benders decomposition for the traveling salesman problem with facility-based drones
Authors: Yuan Yuan, Huan Tang, Jiliu Li, Frederic Semet, Hu Qin
Abstract: This study considers a truck and drone delivery system in which a truck transports parcels from a warehouse either directly to customers or to transshipment facilities, where drones are deployed for last-mile delivery. The problem is modeled as a Traveling Salesman Problem with Facility-based Drones. We propose a mixed-integer programming formulation and a logic-based Benders decomposition (LBBD) algorithm. The master problem determines facility opening, customer assignment to the truck or facilities, and the truck route, while considering only the aggregate flight-distance budget of drones at each facility. The subproblems are formulated using constraint programming and assign deliveries to individual drones while explicitly enforcing drone-level flight-range constraints. Several feasibility and optimality Benders cuts are introduced to strengthen the LBBD algorithm. In addition, valid inequalities are derived to accelerate the master problem and are also embedded in a benchmark branch-and-cut algorithm applied to the arc-flow formulation. An initial heuristic is further developed to quickly provide a high-quality upper bound. Computational experiments demonstrate that the proposed LBBD can solve instances with up to 160 nodes and outperforms both a state-of-the-art commercial solver and the branch-and-cut algorithm in terms of solution quality, computation time, and solvable instance size. Sensitivity analyses further reveal the impact of key parameters and provide valuable managerial insights.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Investigating substitution effects of autonomous taxis using rank-ordered logit models
Authors: Hua Wang, Yutong Cai, Shukai Chen, Dian Sheng
Abstract: In recent years, autonomous vehicles (AVs), particularly in shared mobility applications, have attracted increasing attention from academia, industry, and the general public. However, most existing studies on autonomous taxi services rely on hypothetical stated preference scenarios, as large-scale real-world deployment remains limited. The city-wide operation of Apollo Robotaxis (ARs) in Wuhan, China, provides a unique opportunity to examine traveler responses in a context where autonomous ride-hailing services are widely accessible. Drawing on a stated preference survey that integrates on-site and online data collection, this study investigates how the large-scale deployment of ARs reshapes travel mode choices and competitive dynamics in the urban mobility market. Latent class and random-parameter rank-ordered logit models are employed to capture heterogeneity in traveler preferences. The results reveal substantial variation in willingness to adopt ARs across distinct traveler segments, with cost sensitivity and prior experience playing crucial roles in mode substitution between ARs, traditional taxis, and ride-hailing services. Market simulations further indicate that uniform pricing strategies may lead to uneven impacts across user groups and intensify competitive pressure on conventional drivers, whereas differentiated pricing can promote higher AR adoption while mitigating displacement effects. Overall, the findings highlight the importance of accounting for preference heterogeneity when designing Robotaxi pricing and subsidy policies, and provide empirical evidence to support a more gradual and socially balanced transition toward large-scale autonomous mobility services.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: A general framework for bi-objective user equilibrium with piecewise disutility
Authors: Zhandong Xu, Hongtai Huang, Zhengyang Li, Qianni Wang, Jun Xie
Abstract: This paper proposes a general bi-objective user equilibrium (BUE) framework with piecewise disutility functions for transportation networks. The framework is motivated by empirical evidence that travelers exhibit buffer-threshold behavior, that is, the disutility remains limited within a tolerable range but rises sharply once a critical threshold is exceeded. We introduce a piecewise disutility specification that combines buffer thresholds with flexible post-threshold functional forms, allowing diverse behavioral patterns arising in time–toll trade-offs, electric-vehicle routing, and mean–risk route choice to be modeled within a unified structure. We show that the resulting problem admits a convex optimization formulation and develop a customized column generation algorithm for large-scale computation. Numerical experiments on several real-world networks demonstrate that the proposed framework provides a unified and tractable approach for analyzing bi-objective equilibrium behavior under a range of threshold-based disutility specifications.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Integrating prompt-based zero-shot learning into Bayesian network for maritime cybersecurity risk analysis
Authors: Yunfeng Zhao, Huanhuan Li, Trung Thanh Nguyen, Christian Matthews, Zaili Yang
Abstract: The increasing digitalisation of maritime ecosystems, including vessels, ports, offshore facilities, and shore-based organisations, has expanded the attack surface of maritime operations and increased exposure to cyber threats. Cyber incidents affecting these interconnected systems may propagate across global logistics networks, highlighting the need for systematic cybersecurity risk analysis in maritime transport. However, existing studies often rely on expert judgement or limited datasets, which restrict scalability and hinder comprehensive identification of Risk Influential Factors (RIFs). This study develops a data-driven framework that integrates Large Language Model (LLM)-assisted text classification with Bayesian Network (BN) modelling to analyse maritime cybersecurity risks. A structured taxonomy of RIFs is defined to capture temporal, regional, operational, and technical attributes of cyber incidents. LLM-based prompt engineering is then employed to automatically extract these factors from unstructured incident reports. The reliability of the automated classification process is evaluated through manual annotation on a sampled subset of incident reports and comparative experiments across multiple LLMs. The BN model is further assessed using repeated cross-validation to evaluate predictive performance and robustness. The results reveal key dependencies among cyber incident characteristics and consequence types, providing probabilistic insights into maritime cyber risk patterns. The proposed framework offers a scalable approach for analysing cyber risks in maritime transport systems and supports risk-informed cybersecurity management.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Travel time models incorporating zone boundaries in SBS/RSs with multiple shuttle carriers
Authors: Jingjing Yang, Ran Chen, Hu Yu
Abstract: Shuttle-based Storage and Retrieval Systems equipped with shuttle carriers (SBS/RS-SC) are an emerging alternative to traditional shuttle-based storage and retrieval systems. In SBS/RS-SC, storage racks are partitioned into multiple zones, each comprising several tiers and served by a dedicated shuttle carrier. Unlike conventional shuttles, these carriers can move horizontally and vertically simultaneously, enabling more efficient load transport within each zone. To evaluate the performance of this system, this paper develops closed-form travel time models for both single-command (SC) and dual-command (DC) operating modes. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the developed models approximate the discrete system with high accuracy, with deviations of less than 3.51%. Building on these validated models, a zone boundary optimization model is further proposed to determine the optimal rack partitioning that minimizes expected travel time. The optimization results show that the performance gap between optimal zoning and equal-sized zoning is less than 4.07% for the SC mode and 0.087% for the DC mode, indicating that simplified equal-sized zoning can provide near-optimal performance in practice. Furthermore, sensitivity analysis reveals diminishing returns to improvements in equipment speed, identifies a practical range for the shuttle speed ratio, and shows that the optimal rack layout depends strongly on the interaction between system kinematics and the shape factor. Finally, the framework is extended to incorporate system throughput, investment cost, class-based storage, and alternative dwell-point policies, thereby providing comprehensive decision support for SBS/RS-SC design and operation.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Dynamic resource allocation for managing homeless shelter requests: An approximate dynamic programming approach
Authors: Sina Ansari, Masih Fadaki, Mohammad Delasay
Abstract: Homeless shelters routinely face the challenge of allocating scarce resources to an unpredictable and diverse population with varying levels of need. This paper develops a dynamic, priority-aligned allocation policy for emergency shelter services, modeled as a finite-horizon Markov Decision Process (MDP). We propose an Approximate Dynamic Programming (ADP) approach that incorporates heterogeneous client classes, stochastic arrivals, and capacity constraints, with service performance weighted by policy-driven priority factors. To facilitate implementation, we translate the optimal policy into practical protection-level rules that reserve capacity for higher-priority classes. Using data from the Australian Specialist Homelessness Services Collection, we present a proof-of-concept numerical study with stylized yet data-informed parameter settings that illustrate how the proposed framework can substantially improve performance over benchmark allocation policies, achieving a fill rate of over 95% for high-priority clients, particularly under resource scarcity. The proposed approach offers a practical and interpretable decision-support tool that enables shelter providers to effectively balance priority-based equity and efficiency.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: A decomposition approach for holistic vessel traffic service planning in seaport waters
Authors: Baoli Liu, Yan Huang, De-Ping Yu, Xiaotian Zhuang, Zhongshuai Wang
Abstract: Efficient management of vessel traffic in seaports depends on three closely linked decisions: vessel sequencing, pilot assignment, and tugboat allocation. Traditionally, these decisions are addressed sequentially, resulting in suboptimal or even infeasible vessel traffic service plans. In this study, we consider a joint vessel sequencing, pilot assignment, and tugboat allocation problem (VSPTAP), in which a seaport manages a diverse team of pilots and a heterogeneous fleet of tugboats to service inbound and outbound vessels. We propose a mixed-integer linear programming model for the VSPTAP, which captures the multi-segment navigation structure, channel restrictions, diverse pilotage and tugboat requirements, and the interactions among the three decision layers, with the objective of minimizing the total delay cost of all vessels. While general-purpose solvers suffice for small-scale instances, we propose a decomposition approach to efficiently handle larger and more practical scenarios. The approach partitions the VSPTAP into a master vessel sequencing problem, together with two subproblems for pilot assignment and tugboat allocation, solved via reinforcement learning, column generation, and column enumeration, respectively. These methods are integrated within a hybrid optimization framework that dynamically coordinates vessel sequencing with pilotage and tugboat schedules. Extensive computational experiments based on Qinzhou Port, China, show that the proposed approach substantially outperforms the benchmark methods from the literature and current practices, yielding satisfactory solutions within 15 minutes and enabling daily cost savings of about RMB 232 thousand for the seaport. Furthermore, managerial insights are offered to support the operations and management of seaport traffic.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Behavioral influences in hedging decisions for commodity purchasing
Authors: Maryam Teymoury, Behnam Fahimnia, Andrew Collins
Abstract: Hedging in commodity purchasing involves securing commodity prices or quantities in advance to protect against price fluctuations and reduce financial risk. This paper examines the impact of risk-taking attitude, confidence level, and numeracy skills on a supply manager’s hedging decisions in commodity purchasing. We employ a discrete choice experiment to test four hypotheses grounded in existing literature. The experiment was designed through extensive consultations with industry practitioners and refined through a pilot study. Using data collected from 136 sourcing managers in the fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG) industry, we find that the hedging decisions are significantly influenced by a combination of risk-taking attitude, confidence, and numeracy skills. Risk-taking and confidence are positively associated with riskier hedging choices, while numeracy shows a weaker, negative direct effect, primarily moderated by risk-taking and confidence. These findings deepen our understanding of how specific behavioral traits impact hedging decisions in commodity purchasing, offering practical insights for firms to better align managerial risk preferences with organizational risk management strategies, particularly in volatile market environments.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Trade-offs of recycling strategies under carbon tax and recycling target responsibility system: Trade-in vs. deposit-refund
Authors: Junwei Zhao, Huiqin Zhang, Yexia Zhang, Heli Zhang, Deru Xie, Yuxiang Zhang
Abstract: Under the dual pressures of global climate change and sustainable resource management, carbon taxes and recycling target responsibility systems are synergistically fostering the green transformation of the manufacturing industry through integrated policy combinations. However, optimizing the selection of recycling strategies within reverse logistics under this complex regulatory framework remains a formidable managerial challenge. To explore the operational boundaries of two mainstream recycling strategies, namely Trade-in (TI) and Deposit-refund (DR), we develop a manufacturer-led Stackelberg game model to compare their performance under dual environmental regulations. The findings reveal distinct cost thresholds for strategy selection. TI relies on an internal subsidy mechanism and is particularly effective for products with low production costs and rapid turnover. Its core advantage lies in leveraging discount incentives underpinned by high profit margins to significantly bolster demand for new products. Conversely, DR, which utilizes an external deposit mechanism, yields higher profits in high-cost industries. By externalizing incentive costs, DR maintains a more competitively priced system and effectively steers price-sensitive consumers toward remanufactured products. Interestingly, aligning policy design with the appropriate recycling strategy is key to achieving a triple-win outcome. When production costs are low and carbon taxes are high, TI more effectively balances economic growth, environmental protection, and social welfare. In contrast, DR emerges as the superior choice when production costs are high and carbon taxes are moderate. Our findings provide strategic guidance for firms to optimize recycling choices in reverse logistics and for regulators to orchestrate complementary environmental policies.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Predict-then-optimise interchange control for rail logistics with combined passenger-freight chains
Authors: Elham Ahmadi, André Ludwig, Omid Fatahi Valilai
Abstract: Interchange decisions at rail transfer stations directly affect end-to-end service reliability and cost-to-serve; yet, existing delay-management approaches either forecast delays without prescribing actions or optimise dispatch with coarse delay representations. We propose a predict-then-optimise framework that integrates multi-task LSTM-based delay prediction with a feasibility-constrained Markov Decision Process (MDP) to determine whether to proceed, hold, reschedule, or reroute services at transfer stations. The LSTM models short-horizon delay propagation using only information available at the prediction epoch, while the MDP converts the predicted delay class, capacity regime, infrastructure condition, and bounded dwell feasibility into auditable dispatch recommendations. We evaluate the framework on a three-leg regional rail case study in central Germany comprising lines RB5 (Fulda–Bebra), RB87 (Bebra–Eichenberg), and RB83 (Eichenberg–Kassel), with two physical interchange stations (Bebra and Eichenberg). The results show that the sequence models provide sub-minute ETA accuracy across all three legs and that the Bebra interchange policy reduces the cost-to-serve index by 7.0% relative to the earliest-feasible heuristic while maintaining the same structural miss rate under a 60-minute admissible dwell window. At Eichenberg, the MDP and earliest-feasible policies perform almost identically among evaluable journeys, while the low matched-departure coverage highlights a data and timetable-coordination limitation for full multi-leg evaluation. The framework contributes a deployment-oriented closed-loop architecture in which policy-induced connection gaps are propagated into downstream ETA estimation, supported by per-timestep station embeddings, two-stage cross-leg fine-tuning, and replay-buffer stabilisation. The paper demonstrates how established prediction and control components can be operationally coupled to provide interpretable, manager-facing rail logistics decision support with journey-level KPIs and cost-to-serve reporting.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Vehicle-road-cloud integration: Revolutionizing urban mobility through intelligent transportation systems and advanced traffic flow optimization
Authors: Nok KO, Zhiqin Ma, Changyuan Yu
Abstract: The connection of Vehicles, Road infrastructure and the integration of Cloud computing systems (VRCI) has led to a significant shift in urban transport. The review proposes a new VRCI model that improves urban operations by combining artificial intelligence, the Internet of Things (IOT) and modern network technologies. The paper examines how these elements interact within a within a unified smart city structure. The model focuses on four key innovations that support each other: first, the creation of flexible rules that encourage new technologies while protecting public safety; and second, the use of city-wide sensor networks to gain real-time understanding. Urban activities; third, the application of modern training algorithms to improve traffic; and fourth, ensuring that VRCI development is aligned with the larger objectives of a reasonable city to make more efficient use of resources. Together, these improvements provide a solid foundation for a more efficient and lasting future for cities. The paper also highlighted important challenges, such as data security and the need for global standards. Noting the potential of new tools, such as computing and block chains, to enhance system-wide sustainability. By combining these technical, social and political considerations, it is clear that VIRCI is important not only for improving transport, but also as a key factor in helping cities achieve their sustainable and low-carbon future goals. The study is a practical guide for leaders, researchers and governors who are developing a new generation of smart and liveable cities.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Risk mitigation in perishable supply chains: An AI- driven approach for managing meat distribution
Authors: Bahareh Kargar, Majid Baqeri, Hamed Jahani, Srinivas Talluri
Abstract: The meat supply chain (MSC) faces significant challenges due to the perishability of products, leading to substantial economic and environmental costs. Traditional monitoring and logistics methods often fail to provide real-time predictive insights needed to mitigate spoilage risks. In this study, we propose an artificial intelligence (AI) -driven framework integrating fine-tuned vision-language models (VLMs) – specifically NVILA and Qwen Vision Language (Qwen-VL) – with a robust optimization model for improving freshness prediction and logistics management in MSCs. Using the Meat Freshness Image Dataset, we fine-tune VLMs to classify meat into freshness categories and employ these predictions within a distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model to manage storage, transportation, and spoilage decisions under uncertainty. Our framework leverages Wasserstein-based DRO to model uncertainties in freshness, demand, and transportation times, leading to improved cost efficiency, service levels, and supply chain resilience. Numerical experiments demonstrate that our approach reduces worst-case costs and spoilage compared to nominal optimization methods, offering a scalable and effective solution for perishable supply chain management.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Beggar or enrich-thy-neighbor? Impact of platform cross-border acquisition
Authors: Xiaoran Liu, Xuwei Qin, Lusheng Shao, Xiuqing Gong
Abstract: E-commerce platforms have increasingly pursued cross-border acquisitions in recent years, targeting either foreign online platforms or foreign brick-and-mortar retailers. Motivated by this practice, this paper investigates how the choice of acquisition target reshapes global supply chain dynamics. We develop a game-theoretic model that captures the data-driven network effect associated with acquiring foreign platforms and the in-store service investment and resulting showrooming effect from acquiring foreign retailers. Several findings emerge. First, both acquisition strategies are double-edged swords for the upstream manufacturer.
