Title: A Benders and column generation method to the integrated airline schedule and aircraft recovery with gate reassignment
Authors: Jianlin Jiang, Jiajin Lin, Yan Gu, Yibing Lv, Cheng-Lung Wu
Abstract: Disruptions are inevitable during airline operations, and disruptions cost airlines and the traveling public. Disruption recovery decisions are often made in a sequential process that includes flight rescheduling, aircraft rerouting, crew reassignment, passenger re-accommodation, and gate reassignment for airline operations. Such a sequential recovery approach alleviates the complexity of the whole recovery process but often causes further disruptions to airport gate assignments and high recovery costs for airlines and passengers. This paper presents a novel airline disruption recovery approach by integrating the schedule and aircraft recovery with gate reassignment. We propose a Benders and column generation (BCG) method to solve the integrated problem. By exploiting the favorable structure arising from the Benders decomposition framework, we provide two acceleration techniques for Benders subproblems, a separation technique and an effective infeasibility certificate, to enhance the efficiency of the BCG method. The proposed model is tested on real-world data. In our experiments, all test instances are solved by the BCG method under a five-minute threshold with optimality gaps within 5%. Compared with the sequential recovery approach, the integrated recovery approach significantly saves recovery costs and avoids infeasible gate reassignments caused by the sequential recovery approach.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Editorial: Web 3.0 and Metaverse technologies in logistics and supply chain management
Authors: Liukai Wang, Yu Xiong, Jie Wu, Jason Wang, Hugo K.S. Lam
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: The three-dimensional bin packing problem with variable box size
Authors: Xiangbin Xu, Boyu Wu, Zhongqiang Ma, Yugang Yu
Abstract: Most research on Three-dimensional Bin Packing Problem (3DBPP) treats box size as fixed throughout the packing process. However, in practical packing scenarios, boxes containing garments, bedding items, or plastic foam materials are deformable, exhibiting both compressibility and extensibility. To better capture this reality, we introduce the Three-dimensional Bin Packing Problem with Variable Box Sizes (3DBPP-VBS), which allows changing box sizes during packing. We formulate the problem as a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model and develop a beam search-based algorithm (BSA) for its solution. While Gurobi can obtain optimal solutions for small-scale instances, BSA efficiently generates high-quality near-optimal solutions for larger instances within practical computational times. Extensive experimental results on the Martello and BR instances demonstrate that allowing box size variation significantly enhances space utilization, with improvements of 6.06% in small-size Martello instances and 1.22% in large-size BR instances. Our findings highlight the potential value of considering variable box sizes for improving the efficiency of the 3DBPP, particularly in small-scale scenarios such as packaging operations for express delivery and e-commerce companies.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Optimal design of flexible bus service integrated with trunk transit under demand uncertainty
Authors: Enoch Lee, Tianming Liu, Manzi Li, Hong K. Lo
Abstract: This paper develops a two-stage stochastic optimization framework for designing flexible bus service integrated with trunk transit under uncertain spatial demand. The proposed system jointly supports direct door-to-door service, flexible-to-trunk transfers, and flexible-to-flexible transfers. Passenger willingness to transfer (WTT) is modeled as a demand-partition mechanism, allowing both fixed and service-quality-dependent transfer preferences. To address the strong NP-hardness of the second-stage passenger assignment problem, we develop a reliability-based decomposition method with a tailored trip assignment heuristic for large-scale instances. Numerical experiments based on a Hong Kong case study show that the integrated design reduces total system cost by up to 19.0% relative to a conventional feeder-only flexible-bus-trunk system and by 5.1% relative to a flexible-bus system with ad hoc service. The model also quantifies the value of passenger transfer flexibility, showing that full willingness to transfer can reduce composite system cost by 10.0%. Overall, the results demonstrate the value of jointly coordinating flexible bus deployment, trunk transit integration, and passenger transfer behavior when planning multimodal transit systems under demand uncertainty.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Online task assignment in warehouse considering the pickers’ dynamic capability: A data-driven optimization approach
Authors: Kun Wang, Yunhai Xiang, Wanying Chen
Abstract: Dynamic variations in pickers’ capability are crucial for task assignment efficiency, yet are often overlooked in research due to the focus on system-level optimization and the complexity of modeling human variability. This paper addresses the problem of order fulfillment task assignment considering the pickers’ dynamic capability. A unique feature of the proposed approach is the integration of a data-driven model for characterizing capability with a mixed integer programming optimization model for online task assignment. To solve the model and leverage the pickers’ dynamic capability, we developed a variable time window algorithm based on the proportion of available pickers. Numerical experiments are conducted using data obtained from a warehouse located in Southwest China. The results indicate that our approach significantly improves the accuracy of characterizing pickers’ capability. Additionally, our model modestly reduces total execution time and achieves a notable improvement of over 20% in labor equilibrium. With the help of our model, the warehouse manager can clearly assess the dynamic variations of pickers’ capability and make informed task assignment decisions, ensuring efficient and equitable labor utilization.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Scheduling passenger and freight co-modal transport for a high-speed rail reservation platform: a column-and-row generation-based modular framework
Authors: Xinghan Chen, Weilin Tang, Roel Leus, Xiaoning Zhu
Abstract: High-speed rail (HSR) corridors operating at high frequencies within urban agglomerations often exhibit uneven temporal distribution of passenger volume and imbalanced passenger flows along train trajectories, creating opportunities to expand freight services. To leverage the capacity, we redesign the off-peak ticketing mechanism into a time-slot-based HSR reservation (TRS) platform, through which both passengers and carriers reserve travel sections and receive exact departure times after scheduling. The problem is formulated as a two-layer decision model that integrates line planning and scheduling: the first decision level aligns reservation demand with train stop patterns, while the second decision level refines detailed schedules by accounting for differences in train speeds and priorities. A column-and-row generation–based framework decomposes the problem into modular “carriage-train-schedule” components, dynamically generating candidate carriages and violated constraints to approximate feasible train routes. Numerical experiments across 47 scenarios on both a small-scale corridor and the Yangtze River Delta HSR network show that the proposed algorithm solves five-station instances using only 9.7% of the CPU time required by the Gurobi solver. It also efficiently handles large-scale 37-station network cases involving over 38,065 passenger trips and 2,907 tons of freight in total. Furthermore, under a “weak” passenger-priority principle, TRS enables efficient co-modal transport by increasing operating revenue by 4.88% and passenger seat utilization by 13.05%, while delay penalties account for less than 1% of total revenue. At the same time, operating multi-mode trains during off-peak periods does not result in severe network congestion.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: First-party and third-party complementary apps: investment in research and development, launching, and merger and acquisition
Authors: Tatyana Chernonog, Priel Levy
Abstract: With the enormous growth of app usage and smartphone penetration, an increasing number of third-party developers are offering apps that are complementary to the top-leading core apps, aiming to target the massive audiences of these apps and to enhance the user’s experience. At the same time, top-leading developers may launch their own complementary apps that compete with the third-party apps in terms of quality. The impact of the third-party developer on the first-party developer is twofold: on the one hand, the former creates added value for the core app, which translates into additional profit for the first-party developer. On the other hand, the competition between the first- and third-party substitutable apps calls into question the benefit of launching the first-party substitutable app. At the same time, the third-party developer relies upon the large market of the core app, while his own market share may be eroded due to the competition between the two substitutable apps. In this study, we develop a game-theoretical model of a market consisting of three apps: a core app and two partially substitutable apps that both complement the core app. We investigate the R&D strategies of the developers and derive the conditions under which they choose to launch their complementary apps. In addition, we analyze the M&A strategy of the core-app developer. Several counterintuitive results emerge from the analysis, such as: (i) competition between the two complementary apps can be mutually beneficial; and (ii) a reduction in the quality of the first-party complementary app may, paradoxically, lead to an increase in its demand.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Distributionally robust assortment and inventory optimization with ship-from-store for omnichannel retailers
Authors: Song Jiu, Tianqi Huang
Abstract: Ship-from-store (SFS) has become a prominent initiative for modern retailers to implement an omnichannel strategy. Despite its significant benefits, SFS complicates the coordination of assortment and inventory, which is crucial to enhance the profitability while maintaining the service level. This challenge is aggravated by endogenous complex customer choices across channels and products. To address this challenge, we consider an omnichannel retailer (o-tailer) operating a set of physical stores and relying on SFS to fulfill online demand, and study joint assortment and inventory optimization with SFS over a multi-period sales horizon. We develop separate multinomial logit models for distinct-channel customers to characterize their heterogeneous choice behaviors. Based on partial moment information of market share distributions, we formulate a nonlinear distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model that incorporates customer channel migration. We propose a tractable solution framework that synergistically integrates linearization technique, DRO reformulation, enhanced linear decision rule, and Benders decomposition algorithm, which complement each other to efficiently overcome the computational intractability. The results of extensive numerical experiments suggest that the proposed framework consistently yields high-quality solutions and significantly outperforms several benchmark approaches. We perform sensitivity analyses to investigate the impacts of key parameters on the o-tailer’s financial and operational performance metrics. We further quantity the benefits of implementing distinct store assortments and the SFS program. Some beneficial technical and managerial insights are derived from the empirical findings.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Joint information design and pricing for transportation information service
Authors: Yinlian Zeng, Zili Huang, Qiao-chu He, Xiaoqiang Cai
Abstract: This paper analyzes how a Transportation Information Service (TIS) provider can leverage information design and its associated information service pricing as joint strategic tools to manage traffic congestion. We develop a Bayesian persuasion model for a two-route network with uncertain affine congestion costs, where the provider aims to either minimize the expected total social cost (e.g., a public authority) or maximize profit (e.g., a commercial firm). We compare two fundamental information policies: a common-information policy, which broadcasts the same signal to all subscribers, and a personalized-information policy, which sends private route recommendations. Our results show that providing full information for free is not optimal. Instead, the social-cost-minimizing strategy involves providing full information at a positive price to travelers. Under the assumptions of our model, this strategy also maximizes provider profit, creating an alignment of incentives between a social planner and a commercial entity. Furthermore, while personalized information is superior for congestion mitigation and can achieve the first-best system optimum under certain conditions, we prove a strong profit-equivalence result: the maximum profit achievable under personalized information is identical to that under the simpler common-information policy. Consequently, a profit-seeking provider does not need to invest in complex personalization solely for revenue gains.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Capturing heterogeneous alternative acceptance in route choice behavior using stated choice experiments: a soft truncated choice approach
Authors: Sunghoon Jang, Doosun Hong, Heqing Tan, Anthony Chen
Abstract: Acknowledging that cognitive limitations often prevent travelers from thoroughly evaluating all available route alternatives in complex travel choice situations, this study explores the significance of heterogeneous alternative acceptance in route choice behavior. To address this, Soft Truncated Choice Model (SfTCM) is introduced, along with the derivation of policy indicators to enable a better understanding of the impact of attributes on choice probabilities and market shares. Furthermore, the model’s flexibility and applicability are enhanced through extensions that incorporate heterogeneity and enable incremental model specification by deriving analytical expressions. A carefully designed stated choice experiment on route choice was conducted, systematically varying the number of available alternative routes across different choice sets to assess the heterogeneous impact of choice set size on alternative acceptance. Results demonstrate that individuals do not consistently evaluate all alternatives, as their decisions are influenced by socio-demographics, travel experience, and the number of alternatives presented. The proposed SfTCM consistently outperforms traditional models (MNL and Mixed Logit), offering a more realistic framework for understanding travel decision-making under cognitive constraints. This underscores that choice models assuming full alternative consideration may lead to biased forecasts and suboptimal policy recommendations in transportation; therefore, SfTCM provides a more accurate approach to capture heterogeneous route acceptance for improved travel behavior analysis and transportation policy-making in complex choice situations.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Promoting green port-hinterland transportation: A branch-and-price algorithm for electric truck charging management
Authors: Xiangda Li, Hao Lang, Lingxiao Wu, Changmin Jiang
Abstract: Electric trucks are increasingly deployed for port-hinterland cargo transportation to reduce diesel dependency, yet their charging activities have an important impact on energy costs, transportation efficiency, and grid security. Current research has not yet fully addressed charging management problems that simultaneously account for these multi-dimensional factors. To address the above challenge, this study proposes a novel mixed-integer programming model by considering time-of-use tariffs, demand charge tariffs, and departure delays for charging electric trucks, aiming to minimize time-of-use energy costs, demand charges to reduce peak power demand, and penalty costs associated with departure delays. Then, we reformulate the problem as a set-covering model, and develop a column generation approach to obtain high-quality solutions efficiently. Furthermore, we propose a branch-and-price algorithm to derive the optimal solutions within the reasonable solving time. Numerical experiments on real-world cases are performed to verify the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed solution algorithm. We explore the impacts of the charging power, unit demand charge and unit penalty cost to provide valuable references for managing charging activities of electric trucks within port-hinterland transport systems.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Explicit public and pairwise bandwidth optimization for arterial traffic coordination
Authors: Yu Mei, Tong Wang, Lei Wei, Yu Han
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Robust home healthcare routing problem and resource assignment considering robot collaboration and service disruptions: A hybrid Benders and column generation method
Authors: Behrouz Mohammadi-Kordkheili, Rashed Sahraeian
Abstract: Home healthcare involves medical and caregiving services for patients at home. Coordinating a multi-skilled workforce and managing consumable and non-consumable resources pose challenges. Poor service quality can lead to disruptions, necessitating rework in service delivery. To address these issues, we propose a two-echelon home healthcare routing problem considering personnel collaboration and service disruptions. The first echelon involves a routing problem with multi-skilled workers and resource allocation. The home healthcare center and vehicles have capacity limits for transporting workers and resources. New technologies, such as care robots, assist caregivers and reduce service times. Since services may face disruptions, an additional routing problem is formulated to handle reworking services in the second echelon. On the other hand, service quality, travel time, and service time are influenced by randomness and box uncertainties. To deal with this, we propose a robust stochastic-box programming, solved through a combination of genetic algorithm (GA), column generation (CG), and Benders decomposition (BD). GA is used as the initial solution for CG, while BD is applied to solve the subproblem of CG. The proposed method is evaluated by solving 50 instances, with the results demonstrating its superiority. To assess robustness, the deviation coefficient and uncertainty level are increased in a case study, leading to reduced risk. Finally, three managerial sensitivity analyses showed that enhancing worker skill scores improved service quality, increasing absences raised service completion time, and replacing vehicles with lower-cost drivers decreased the objective function by 15%.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Make waves: quantifying the impact of the Red Sea crisis on global container port turnaround time
Authors: Mingzheng Liu, Kee-hung Lai, Yuanzhe Liu, Christina W.Y. Wong, Jiayi Chen, Zaili Yang
Abstract: The Red Sea crisis, a major maritime disruption event, has attracted widespread attention. This crisis disrupted global shipping networks, increased voyage distances, and caused delayed cargo deliveries. As critical nodes in maritime transport, ports may experience operational disruptions from typical maritime events. While anecdotal evidence suggests substantial port-level effects, rigorous empirical evidence remains limited. To address this gap, this study utilises global Automatic Identification System (AIS) data to calculate port turnaround time (PTT) for the top 100 container ports. Then, we apply Difference-in-Differences (DID) and Regression Discontinuity Design-Difference-in-Differences (RDD-DID) models to capture the sustained average effect and immediate impact of the crisis on PTT. Both methods isolate seasonal and cyclical influences during the observation period. Our analysis shows that the crisis increased ports’ PTT in both models, with results that satisfy the parallel trends assumption as validated through event study methodology. Employing the same testing procedures combining DID, RDD-DID, and event study approaches, we further identify the route-based regions affected by the Red Sea crisis. The results indicate that the impacts varied across regions. For the affected regions, we also conduct heterogeneity analyses which reveal significant immediate and sustained PTT escalations across large ports and ports with automated terminal. Further analysis of the PTT sub-metrics reveals that berthing operation time (BOT) experienced both immediate and sustained increases, whereas waiting for berth time (WBT) exhibited only a significant sustained increase following the Red Sea crisis. This study provides evidence that crises at critical maritime chokepoints can propagate to the port sector. These findings provide valuable insights for shipping companies and ports, enabling them to proactively mitigate the negative impacts of such disruptions and to enhance their responsiveness and flexibility when confronting similar crises in the future.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Model-assisted multi-agent reinforcement learning for collaborative synchromodal transport re-planning under service time uncertainty
Authors: Xiaoyu Luo, Yimeng Zhang, Mi Gan, Xiaobo Liu, Bilge Atasoy
Abstract: Synchromodal transport operations frequently require rapid re-planning in response to uncertain terminal service times, yet such decisions are typically made by multiple carriers with heterogeneous objectives and decentralized control. This study investigates collaborative re-planning in synchromodal transport networks under service-time uncertainty from a multi-carrier perspective. We formulate the problem as a decentralized decision-making process in which carriers must coordinate re-planning actions while preserving individual rationality. To address this challenge, we propose a model-assisted multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework that combines heuristic plan generation with learning-based carrier coordination. An adaptive large neighborhood search (ALNS) heuristic is used to generate feasible candidate re-planning options, while carriers are modeled as learning agents that decide whether to accept or reject these options through a consensus mechanism. Rather than directly optimizing a centralized model, carriers learn acceptance policies based on local observations and realized outcomes, without requiring prior knowledge of service-time distributions. An event-triggered and regret-based learning scheme is introduced to align global delay mitigation with carrier-specific cost preferences under uncertainty. Extensive computational experiments on a realistic synchromodal transport network demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly improves re-planning performance compared with benchmark strategies. The results show that decentralized, heterogeneous multi-agent coordination can outperform centralized and homogeneous approaches, particularly in scenarios with high uncertainty and avoidable delays. Mechanism and ablation analyses further reveal the structural importance of multi-agent decomposition, carrier heterogeneity, and the temporal allocation of decision preferences along the transport chain. Additional analyses examine sensitivity to key reward hyperparameters and negotiation round limits, robustness under alternative disruption distributions and network-graph perturbations, and controlled extension settings with more carriers and transshipments. The proposed approach provides a practical decision-support methodology for collaborative synchromodal transport re-planning under uncertainty.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Collective adoption challenges in maritime digital platforms: a multi-stakeholder perspective
Authors: Fangli Zeng, Shuning Zheng, Qifeng Wang, Shuojiang Xu, Hing Kai Chan
Abstract: Digital platforms are widely promoted for improving coordination, visibility, and data exchange in maritime logistics. Yet many platform initiatives struggle to achieve sustained and widespread engagement in practice. This study explains why digital platforms struggle to achieve collective adoption among multiple stakeholders involved in maritime logistics, including different tiers of freight forwarders, shippers, and manufacturers. Using a qualitative research design, this study identifies a cascade of misfits between platform design assumptions and the institutional and operational structures of the industry. These misfits propagate at the platform design, collective adoption, and organizational implementation levels, ultimately leading to fragmented and selective platform use. The findings reveal that adoption is constrained not simply by technological limitations but by systemic misalignments across actors, roles, workflows, and governance arrangements. This study contributes to the logistics and supply chain literature by explaining why digital platforms fail to scale in asset-intensive environments and by identifying the conditions, such as shared standards, interoperability, and cross-actor alignment, that are needed to enable meaningful digital transformation in maritime logistics.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: A consensus fixing based heuristic for liner shipping network design with stochastic demands
Authors: Mikkel Linneberg Lassen, David Pisinger
Abstract: Meeting sustainability goals in maritime shipping requires designing route networks that utilize vessel capacity effectively, while accommodating fluctuating container demand. To address uncertainty from seasonal demand variations, we study the two-stage stochastic liner shipping network design problem, where first-stage decisions define the network structure and second-stage decisions route containers across demand scenarios. We propose the first generic solution approach capable of solving stochastic Liner Shipping Network Design Problem instances of real-world scale from LINER-LIB, including networks with up to 202 ports and 9615 demand commodities. Our method introduces a novel population-based metaheuristic using consensus fixing : in parallel for each scenario, the first-stage decisions are solved with an ALNS framework, while second-stage flow decisions are evaluated using fast column generation. The scenarios iteratively attempt to reach consensus on fixing a first-stage decision based on various score and scale functions. To handle the complexity of the first-stage decision space, we introduce a relaxed decision representation when applying consensus fixing. This enables a convenient extension of the framework to non-binary problems and generates a structured solution population with preferred common features, supported by dedicated population management mechanisms. Computational experiments demonstrate that the method finds high-quality solutions within reasonable time, achieving improvements of up to 20–30% compared to a deterministic baseline. The results also reveal that the value of stochastic planning is instance-dependent: flexible network structures benefit substantially, while single-hub instances show minimal advantage from stochastic optimization due to their limited routing adaptability.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Cross-border e-commerce platform strategy design and analysis: Reselling versus agency
Authors: Wenbin Liu, Haohan Xiao, Ting Qu
Abstract: Considering a cross-border e-commerce (CBEC) market involving multiple players of a CBEC platform, the supplier, and consumers, where the CBEC platform integrates the cross-border logistics services to connect the supplier and consumers. To investigate whether the CBEC platform can effectively promote the CBEC service, we deploy the game-theoretic approach to establish two business models without and with the CBEC platform. The model with the CBEC platform is designed by two channel strategies, namely, the reselling strategy and the agency strategy. The platform in the reselling strategy acts as a reseller and procures products from the supplier, while the platform in the agency strategy serves as a third-party entity to benefit the supplier for self-stores. Equilibrium results concerning the CBEC platform’s profit, the supplier’s profit, and consumer surplus can be derived from the two models. The merits of integrating CBEC services can be obtained by comparing the results of the two models. Results show that the model with the CBEC platform outperforms the model without the platform in terms of promoting the supplier’s profit and consumer surplus. Findings regarding which channel strategy should be implemented for the CBEC platform can also be obtained, where the reselling strategy should be chosen when the commission rate is low while the agency strategy should be chosen otherwise. Further findings show that several factors, e.g., the tax tariff, the investment cost coefficient, and the service level coefficient, will also affect the final results. Managerial implications regarding promoting CBEC platform operations are proposed and discussed lastly, including customizing CBEC channel strategies for targeted markets/regions, increasing the commission rate, and enhancing the CBEC platform’s services.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Dynamic pricing optimization for waste recycling networks: a spatiotemporal incentive framework
Authors: Lingyu Meng, Xiaohang Zhu, Najmaddin Akhundov, Zhijie Sasha Dong, Ayesha Saeed, Waqas Ahmed
Abstract: The global plastic waste crisis demands innovative recycling solutions that are both economically viable and operationally efficient. Traditional recycling networks, often relying on uniform pricing and decentralized decision-making, frequently suffer from spatial imbalances, facility congestion, and prohibitive collection costs. This paper tackles these challenges by introducing a spatiotemporal dynamic pricing framework designed for plastic waste recycling, utilizing existing retail gas stations as decentralized collection hubs. Unlike conventional models that address pricing, facility location, and route in isolation, the proposed approach co-optimizes these decisions within a unified model under explicit capacity and regulatory constraints. A pivotal innovation involves the development of a consumer choice model that explicitly captures the trade-off between financial incentives and travel distance – a behavioral nuance often oversimplified in prior literature. The resulting complex optimization problem is reformulated into a computationally tractable mixed-integer linear program through a linearization technique. The framework’s efficacy is rigorously validated via extensive numerical experiments and a large-scale case study centered on Houston’s Loop 610 corridor. Results demonstrate that the proposed location-based pricing strategy yields a statistically significant enhancement in net profitability and achieves a 46.3% reduction in collection costs compared to a conventional uniform pricing strategy, while simultaneously ensuring regulatory compliance and mitigating localized congestion. This research provides an actionable and scalable decision-support tool, underscoring that the integrated optimization of incentives and logistics via existing infrastructure is instrumental for improving recycling performance, reducing operational expenditures, and advancing the transition toward a circular economy for plastics.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Learning-based route-speed optimization for emission-control-area-aware sailing: No backfire to green shipping
Authors: Yuhan Guo, Yiyang Wang, Xiaonan Zhang, Shihao Li, Lingxiao Wu
Abstract: While serving as a cost-efficient backbone supporting intensive intercontinental product exchanges, the shipping industry nevertheless releases considerable quantities of greenhouse gases (GHGs) and sulfur pollutants. In response to the shipping-introduced environmental deterioration, relevant regulatory measures have been implemented by the International Maritime Organization (IMO), particularly emphasizing the designation of emission control areas (ECAs). Compliance with ECA regulations through fuel oil changeover leads to higher per-voyage operating costs, thereby compelling shipping companies to seek profitability-sustaining strategies. However, conventional ECA-aware navigation optimization, typically formulated through shorter routes and reduced speeds within those waters, attains cost savings at the inevitable expense of increased overall GHG emissions. Although ECAs are not specifically instituted for GHG control, the inherent conflict between policymakers and stakeholders, driven by their divergent environmental and operational priorities, can compel this regulation to backfire against the IMO’s overarching green shipping goals. Meanwhile, these route-speed decisions, driven exclusively by cost minimization, may undermine a ship’s adherence to prescribed arrival time windows, triggering delay penalties that offset anticipated cost efficiencies, and even causing supply chain disruptions. Accordingly, this study proposes a learning-based predict-then-optimize framework that generates diversified sailing plans for ECA-involved voyages, enabling the reconciliation of green shipping goals with operational interests. To deliver tangible emission reductions without sacrificing commercial viability, related constraints are integrated into a cost- and time-oriented Pareto optimization model, imposing explicit GHG bounds on the decision space, rather than merely exploring policy-compliant route-speed configurations under ECA regulations. Building upon the meticulously-engineered data-driven prediction model and learning-aided optimization algorithm, our framework greatly outperforms other state-of-the-art counterparts, as empirically validated by real-world case studies.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Energy-aware integrated order assignment and routing for heterogeneous couriers in on-demand delivery
Authors: Xian Guo, Zhiyuan Wang, Xiaoyu Ma, Yuli Zhang, Lun Ran, Yucai Yang
Abstract: On-demand delivery (ODD) platforms increasingly rely on heterogeneous courier workforces (in-house, supplementary dedicated, and crowdsourced couriers) to meet stringent time-window requirements. Among these types, crowdsourced couriers -the workforce backbone -predominantly utilize battery-swapping two-wheeled electric vehicles (TWEVs) to sustain high-frequency operations. In the face of these evolving characteristics, however, real-world operational practices reveal a critical gap: current dispatching systems often manage in-house couriers, supplementary dedicated couriers, and crowdsourced couriers through separate decision processes rather than a unified system-level mechanism, while also overlooking energy-logistics couplings, including energy-constrained order assignments, speed variations dependent on state of charge (SoC) and mandatory detours for battery swapping. Such fragmented dispatching practices and omitted energy considerations frequently lead to unexecutable plans and delivery delays. To address this, we propose an energy-aware integrated order assignment and routing model that unifies the dispatching of heterogeneous courier workforces by explicitly incorporating SoC-dependent travel speeds and battery swapping detours. To solve this computationally challenging problem, we design a nested tabu search algorithm based on a bi-level “fast search-precise evaluation” structure. The outer level conducts fast global assignment search with an incremental routing heuristic, while the inner level incrementally solves courier-level mixed-integer programming (MIP)-based routing subproblems to ensure accurate cost evaluation. Extensive experiments using real-world data demonstrate that our algorithm yields high-quality solutions efficiently, accelerating computation by 2–3 orders of magnitude over Gurobi with a 1.6% average gap, whereas traditional tabu search and adaptive large neighborhood search (ALNS) exhibit substantially larger average gaps of over 12%. Crucially, the proposed framework significantly outperforms conventional dispatching strategies that neglect energy-related constraints. Furthermore, sensitivity analyses provide managerial insights into how increasing swap-cabinet availability, expanding crowdsourced capacity, improving battery efficiency and capacity, and adjusting low-battery thresholds can enhance system efficiency. Overall, this study paves the way for sustainable and reliable urban delivery systems.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Delayed matching strategies in demand-responsive transit: The role of market thickness
Authors: Haomiao Wang, Haonan He, Haoxiang Yang
Abstract: Tidal demand in cross-regional travel can cause peak-period shortages and off-peak underutilization in fixed-route transit. Although Demand-Responsive Transit (DRT) offers greater flexibility, its performance depends critically on when requests are matched and how delayed matching is coordinated with passenger pooling and meeting points (MPs). We formulate this problem as an event-driven Semi-Markov Decision Process that accounts for stochastic request arrivals and heterogeneous expected pickup times (EPTs). In pairwise settings, we show that the optimal delayed-matching policy follows a threshold structure determined by the time remaining until a passenger’s EPT and the required pickup travel time. We then develop the Dynamic Threshold and Market Thickness (DTMT) strategy for pooled services and further integrate it with spatiotemporal MP clustering to obtain MP-DTMT. Numerical experiments and a case study based on MTA Line 646 show that DTMT consistently outperforms Greedy and Batching benchmarks, while MP-DTMT further reduces total cost by 37.8%–46.1%. The results reveal how market thickness increases the value of waiting, whereas MP coordination preserves temporal flexibility by reducing pickup travel requirements. This study provides interpretable dynamic-matching strategies for DRT systems facing volatile tidal demand.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Collaborative routing orchestration for organic food distribution
Authors: Daniel Ocampo-Giraldo, Ana María Anaya-Arenas, Walid Klibi, Janosch Ortmann
Abstract: This paper investigates the Collaborative Routing Orchestration for Organic Food Distribution Problem (CRO-FDP), a two-echelon collaborative distribution network setting inspired by a regional organic food network in Quebec, Canada. The CRO-FDP integrates hub selection, vehicle routing and synchronisation decisions under tight time constraints to coordinate multiple producers and food banks sharing logistics resources. We develop a mixed-integer model and a time-expanded reformulation that jointly capture routing and timing decisions across a discretised planning horizon. A dedicated Relax-Solve-and-Fix matheuristic leverages this reformulation to efficiently solve realistic instances beyond the reach of standard formulations. Computational experiments demonstrate that the time-expanded model consistently yields feasible and near-optimal solutions for medium and large instances, outperforming the compact formulation. Results reveal significant efficiency and sustainability gains: collaborative pooling and hub usage reduce total travel distance by up to 1,000 km (an average decrease of 28%) and lower fleet requirements while maintaining service quality. These findings emphasise the strategic value of orchestration and hub-based collaboration for enhancing the environmental and economic performance of regional food distribution systems.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Cooperative path optimization for MULTI-AGV systems in high-density warehousing based on a spatio-temporal coupling conflict probability field
Authors: Tingping Feng, Yunhai Xiang, Yangxin Teng, Xinchen Tang, Junmin Li, Simon X. Yang, Ming Jian
Abstract: Addressing the critical challenges of spatio-temporal conflict resolution and global optimization in dynamic path planning for multiple Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) in high-density warehouse logistics environments, this paper innovatively proposes a closed-loop cooperative path optimization method fusing “conflict probability prediction, neural-dynamics-based modulation, and dynamic deadlock resolution”. First, a Spatio-Temporal Coupling Conflict Probability Field (STC-CPF) model based on Gaussian diffusion is constructed. This model integrates the temporal evolution of AGV motion states with spatial diffusion characteristics to quantitatively predict potential conflict risks. Second, a neural-dynamics-based path generator is designed. A conflict-goal dual-gain excitation function is proposed, and the STC-CPF is embedded into the excitation mechanism of a Glasius bio-inspired neural network (GBNN) to achieve cooperative optimization of conflict avoidance and path smoothing, effectively overcoming the defect of traditional GBNN falling into local optima. Furthermore, a Dynamic Priority Deadlock Break Strategy (DPDBS) is proposed, which realizes real-time priority adjustment and deadlock avoidance through a dynamic weighting mechanism combining conflict threat levels and task progress. In experimental validations of multi-AGV collaborative scenarios, the proposed method reduces path length, turning frequency, and turning angle by up to 14.53%, 58.62%, and 68.75%, respectively, compared with contrast algorithms. Compared with benchmark strategies, operational efficiency is improved by approximately 37.05%, and the conflict occurrence rate is reduced by 50%. The results indicate that the proposed method can significantly enhance the safety and operational efficiency of multi-AGV systems in high-density dynamic environments, providing an efficient and reliable solution for collaborative operations in intelligent warehouse logistics systems.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Dynamic truck-drone collaborative routing with stochastic requests under changing weather conditions
Authors: Shan Zhao, Jian Zhang, Leandro C. Coelho
Abstract: While drones are revolutionizing logistics services by enabling more efficient, environmentally friendly operations, their operations are highly susceptible to weather disruptions. This paper investigates a dynamic truck-drone routing problem with stochastic requests and wind conditions. To enable efficient real-time decision-making and high customer responsiveness, we formulate the problem as a Markov decision process and propose an approximate dynamic programming (ADP) algorithm. Based on the value function approximation scheme and a truck-drone collaborative routing heuristic, the ADP algorithm manages request acceptance, order assignment, and route planning instantly upon the arrival of each new request. To account for the impact of wind on drone operations, we study the mathematical relationship between the wind’s direction and speed and the drone’s airspeed, course, and ground speed. The incorporation of this relationship into the ADP algorithm yields a robust energy-consumption management strategy that can ensure successful drone sorties under changing wind conditions. Computational experiments validate the algorithm’s efficiency on instances with nearly 300 requests. The results indicate a substantial increase in order acceptance rates compared to the benchmark approaches that ignore wind impacts. Specifically, wind-aware routing increases the number of accepted requests by 18.58% compared to wind-unaware approaches. These findings demonstrate that integrating real-time weather data effectively enhances operational reliability and service capacity of drone-assisted logistics.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Joint planning of vertiports and backup landing sites for urban air mobility networks
Authors: Zhonghao Zhao, Kai Wang, Wei Zhang, Shulu Chen, Xiaobo Qu
Abstract: Urban air mobility (UAM) represents a transformative shift in urban transportation. However, its operational safety within low-altitude urban environments remains a paramount concern that may undermine public acceptance and hinder practical implementation. To improve system resilience and safety, this paper proposes a joint planning model for vertiports and backup landing sites (BLSs) that explicitly incorporates safety considerations into UAM network design. Specifically, the model simultaneously optimizes vertiport and BLS locations, flight route establishment, and BLS assignments, capturing the interdependencies between strategic network planning and contingency landing scenarios. To evaluate network-level safety performance, we develop a generalized safety cost framework based on a set of generated contingency landing events (CLEs) along UAM flight routes. The framework quantifies multiple dimensions of safety impact, including diversion time, low-altitude airspace conflicts, and disruptions to ground passengers. The overall planning objective is to minimize the total network safety cost while satisfying the UAM demand coverage requirements and service constraints. A comprehensive case study based on real-world travel demand data from Beijing is conducted to demonstrate the applicability of the proposed framework. Sensitivity analysis is also performed to explore the impact of several key planning parameters on system performance. The findings highlight the necessity of incorporating safety as a primary consideration in early-stage UAM network planning and provide practical insights for designing safe UAM systems.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Clarifying the Intersections of Visibility, Traceability, and Transparency: A Data-Centric Framework for Supply Chain Management
Authors: Wei Nie, Naoum Tsolakis, Manoj Dora, Mukesh Kumar
Abstract: Global supply chains (SCs) face critical vulnerabilities from disruptions, regulatory changes, and sustainability pressures, increasing the need for robust data and information processing capabilities to support end-to-end coordination and accountability. Visibility, traceability, and transparency across end-to-end SCs are intended to address these challenges, yet they are often used interchangeably. This creates ambiguity about which SC data elements, such as demand patterns, inventory levels and material flow records, are required and how these data should be analysed to operationalise these capabilities effectively. This study conducts a combined narrative review of 32 conceptual definitions and a systematic review of 72 empirical studies to develop a data-centric framework that clarifies the concepts of SC visibility, traceability, and transparency from a data perspective. Findings reveal that: (i) visibility requires real-time operational data to support operational decisions; (ii) traceability demands historical, product-level data to enable retrospective analysis (tactical decisions); and (iii) transparency necessitates contextual disclosure data for stakeholder accountability (strategic decisions). This research contributes to the Operations Management field by defining SC visibility, traceability, and transparency as distinct information-processing capabilities enabled by specific data requirements. A proposed data-centric framework supports SC managers in identifying data gaps, aligning data requirements and pertinent investments with strategic objectives, and designing SC stakeholder-specific implementation pathways.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Robust train timetabling based on realized operations: a data-driven prediction-optimization framework
Authors: Ping Huang, Andrea D’Ariano, Yuxiang Yang, Gongyuan Lu, Zhongcan Li, Francesco Corman
Abstract: Recovery times in train timetables are the main resources to absorb train delays and hinder train delay propagation. Train timetables should be robust to reduce train delays and hinder delay propagation as much as possible, given the stochastic nature of both. Train operation data reflects the performance of published timetables, allowing us to optimize them based on that performance. This study presents a framework considering train delays and delay propagation in the train operation process to optimize the train timetable from a data-driven perspective. The proposed model contains three components, including an initial delays distribution (ID) model to describe delays at the origin station due to vehicle connection or passengers, a delay propagation (DP) model containing a distribution and prediction model to describe train delay increases and reduction in train operations, respectively, and a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) model to optimize the recovery time allocation in the timetable. The model aims to maximize the expected reduction in train delay, subject to constraints on train operational safety and infrastructure occupation. The DRL model achieves the maximum return/objective by greedily exploring in the simulation environment and consistently interacting with the ID and DP model. Real-world cases with diverse scales, based on operational data and published timetables for Chinese high-speed railways, were used to evaluate the performance of the proposed model. Comparative analyses were conducted to evaluate the performance of the published timetable, optimal solution, practical rules/heuristics, and other widely used data-driven timetable optimization models. Experimental results show that the proposed model, on average, produced 23.8%, 10.5%, and 30.5% improvements over the published timetable, the best practical rules/heuristics, and the best data-driven timetable optimization models, respectively, with an average gap of less than 5.3% to the optimal solution. Finally, the proposed model can quickly compute a new timetable with over 100 trains (in 6 seconds), demonstrating its high efficiency and applicability.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Electric vehicle charging station location selection using generative artificial intelligence
Authors: Eun Hak Lee, Euntak Lee
Abstract: As electric vehicle (EV) adoption increases, ensuring efficient and well-distributed charging infrastructure has become a critical challenge. While many EV charging station location problem (CSLP) studies focus on minimizing costs or travel distance, it is crucial to consider the surrounding geospatial characteristics of existing stations that influence operational performance. This study proposes a generative artificial intelligence (GenAI)-based framework that integrates high-dimensional EV-related geospatial data, including EV usage, land-use, population, and traffic attributes. We incorporate a variational autoencoder (VAE) and a graph convolutional network (GCN) into the model to capture similarities among existing charging stations, and to identify suitable locations for future stations. The VAE compresses high-dimensional EV input data into a low-dimensional latent space, and the GCN uses this latent representation to predict locations suitable for charging stations. Using real-world data from Bryan–College Station, Texas, US, the proposed model outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving an F1-score of 0.87 in distinguishing existing station locations from non-station locations. The model also identifies 27 additional candidate locations that show geospatial characteristics similar to those of existing stations, based on a similarity value. We further evaluate two policy implementation scenarios, maximizing geospatial similarity and minimizing total travel distance, each yielding different outcomes aligned with distinct strategic objectives. The findings highlight the importance of incorporating spatial context into CSLP and provide insights for future EV infrastructure planning, promoting both efficiency and accessibility in the growing electric mobility sector.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Drone pre-positioning and scheduling for emergency response in ports
Authors: Bo Lu, Manni Cong, Guowei Zhang
Abstract: In recent years, ports have become increasingly congested and operationally complex with the expansion of global maritime trade, making effective emergency response to frequent low-severity incidents critical. Drones offer a promising solution for rapid response in large-scale container terminals by enabling fast access and reducing surveillance blind spots. Motivated by this potential, we study a drone-based pre-positioning and scheduling problem for port emergency response under uncertainty. To address stochastic accident arrivals and service times, we develop an entropy-based robust satisficing model that jointly determines pre-positioning and operational scheduling decisions within a P-Queue framework. Numerical experiments on a container terminal, including a case drawn from Nansha Port in China, demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently outperforms benchmark methods in out-of-sample performance.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: A synchronized framework for straw recycling logistics
Authors: Yi-Jia Wang, Jiaqi Zhou, Yao Cheng, Jian An, George Q. Huang
Abstract: Straw, as a byproduct of agricultural production, is used in resource-oriented, feed-oriented, and substrate-oriented ways, while straw recycling is the first step toward its efficient utilization. In practice, straw recycling enterprises first determine the baling plan and then the transport plan. Such a sequential decision-making method increases the time delay between these two processes and the maximum completion time. However, existing studies have rarely taken this issue into account. This study proposes an integrated scheduling framework to synchronize straw baling and transportation by jointly determining the working routes of straw balers and transporters, and proposes an efficient solution algorithm to solve it. Numerical experiments using real-world datasets show that our proposed methodology provides high-quality solutions within a reasonable computation time and reduces the maximum completion time, compared with the sequential decision-making method. Expanding the fleets of straw balers and transporters shortens the maximum completion time, and more straw balers also significantly decrease waiting time.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: A two-phase lexicographic optimization framework for fleet sizing and routing in electric vehicle routing problems
Authors: Jingwei Wang, Kechen Ouyang, Yaoxin Wu, Jie Gao
Abstract: This paper presents an electric vehicle routing problem with time windows and partial recharging (EVRPTW-PR) in which both the fleet size and the routing plan are decision variables. In many applications, the number of electric vehicles is a tactical decision that drives long-term investments in vehicles, chargers, and drivers, whereas routing is an operational decision made day-to-day for a given fleet. To support decisions at both levels, we formulate EVRPTW-PR with a lexicographic objective, in which we first determine the minimum number of vehicles needed to serve all customers within their time windows under battery and capacity constraints, and then we optimize the total travel distance for that fleet size. To solve this computational challenging problem efficiently, we propose a two-phase adaptive large neighborhood search (ALNS) tailored to this lexicographic structure. In addition, to further reduce computation and guide the search, we develop a supervised learning model that maps instance descriptors to a recommended fleet size. This model replaces the burdensome ALNS for fleet size reduction and warm-starts the second-phase ALNS. Numerical experiments on standard EVRPTW-PR benchmarks show that the designed two-phase ALNS framework improves a state-of-the-art ALNS, and that the learning-enhanced variant reduces the average fleet size by about 0.24 vehicles per instance with very similar travel distances, including under stochastic demand perturbations.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Feasibility assessment in attended home delivery with basket uncertainty
Authors: Liana van der Hagen, Niels Agatz, Remy Spliet
Abstract: In attended home delivery, retailers usually let customers select a delivery time slot for receiving their orders. The delivery capacity, i.e., the number of vehicles and drivers, is often fixed and inflexible in the short term. To effectively use their delivery capacity, e-grocers may dynamically choose not to offer a particular time slot to arriving customers, given the already accepted customer orders. One complicating factor is that online grocers allow customers to change their order basket at any time before the cut-off. Consequently, the e-grocer is uncertain about how much vehicle capacity should be reserved for each of the customers during the booking process. We study the challenges associated with this basket size uncertainty. To address these, we propose fast strategies based on heuristics and machine learning that use basket size scenarios to perform probabilistic feasibility evaluations and evaluate their effectiveness on the system-level performance.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Last-mile delivery problem with flexible time slot and location options under stochastic customer behavior
Authors: Ze Zhou, Fangting Zhou, Jiaming Wu, Balázs Kulcsár
Abstract: The growth of e-commerce has led to a significant rise in daily parcel deliveries, placing increasing pressure on logistics services. Although various delivery options, including home and out-of-home delivery, are offered to enhance customer availability, uncertainty in customer preferences regarding delivery locations and time slots further complicates delivery operations. In this paper, we introduce a last-mile delivery problem with flexible delivery options under stochastic customer behavior, formulated as a two-stage stochastic programming model. The novelty of our model lies in the integration of comprehensive delivery options, including various locations and time slots, with pricing decisions. Furthermore, we incorporate heterogeneous customer preferences across mixed delivery options. To efficiently solve the problem, we develop a hybrid adaptive large neighborhood search (h-ALNS) heuristic based on scenario simulations. Extensive numerical experiments demonstrate the advantages of the mixed delivery strategy and confirm the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. Our numerical analysis offers important managerial insights for optimizing last-mile delivery assortment and pricing, particularly in addressing customer uncertainty.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Electric truck-based robot delivery problem with nonlinear charging
Authors: Shaohua Yu, Tengkuo Zhu, Jakob Puchinger
Abstract: This study addresses an electric truck-based robot collaborative delivery problem that incorporates the inherently nonlinear charging behavior of both vehicle types. A mixed-integer linear programming model with piecewise linear charging representation is developed, and its solution approach is enhanced by time-dependent valid inequalities and tailored heuristics. Numerical experiments show that the proposed methods efficiently generate high-quality solutions across diverse urban logistics scenarios. The results indicate that partial charging strategies consistently outperform full charging, and that assuming linear charging may yield infeasible or misleading solutions in practice. Sensitivity analyses further reveal that system performance is most influenced by battery capacity and the number of charging stations, whereas variations in charging rates have comparatively minor effects.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Designing flexible service strategies for urban drone Delivery: A hybrid Simulation-Optimization framework
Authors: Zhijie Yang, Fei Ma, Yu Wang, Qing Liu, Qipeng Sun, Gangyan Xu, Wei Ren
Abstract: Urban drone delivery offers the potential to improve last-mile logistics efficiency, yet it introduces challenges in resource allocation and dynamic pricing under uncertain operational conditions. This study proposes a flexible service strategy design (FSSD) framework that integrates system dynamics (SD) modeling with reinforcement learning (RL) to enable adaptive deployment and pricing decisions. The SD model captures nonlinear feedback mechanisms and time-varying interactions within the delivery system, while a Deep Q-Network (DQN) is employed to learn pricing and resource allocation strategies that adapt to real-time fluctuations in demand and system constraints. A case study based on Meituan’s drone delivery pilot in Shenzhen, China, demonstrates a 14.88% increase in average daily cumulative profit along with a significant reduction in backlog volatility. The learned strategies are responsive to environmental variations and generalize effectively across different system states. Sensitivity analyses and extended experiments on economies of scale and dynamic pricing further identify key drivers of performance. The FSSD framework offers actionable managerial insights for designing adaptive, scalable, and efficient drone logistics systems.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: A stochastic tri-level interdiction model for relief train location and infrastructure protection
Authors: Florentina Hager, Melanie Reuter-Oppermann
Abstract: Deploying relief trains as part of disaster response plans can be a promising strategy to enhance transport capacity and potentially improve survival chances in large-scale disasters. However, the limited availability of relief trains, combined with uncertainties in demand prediction and potential infrastructure damage, necessitates both strategic positioning of relief trains and robust protective interventions for infrastructure. Addressing these challenges, we introduce a tri-level Defender-Attacker-Defender interdiction problem. In this model, the defender determines train placement and infrastructure protection, while the attacker, representing either a hostile agent or the worst-case realization of a natural disruption, interdicts unprotected network arcs. During the response phase, trains are routed to disaster sites and operational medical facilities. Considering the inherent uncertainties in disasters, our approach incorporates scenario-dependent disruptions and evaluates multiple scenarios during the attacker-stage. To solve the problem, we propose a progressive hedging-inspired algorithm. We apply it to a test set of instances and two real-world-inspired instances for the country of Austria and France and discuss the impact of algorithmic choices.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Seismic resilience enhancement of EMS system under hospital functional uncertainty: a multi-stage location-assignment-treatment stochastic programming approach
Authors: Shunshun Pei, Changhai Zhai, Jin Liu, Chenyu Zhang
Abstract: This study proposes a resilience-driven optimization framework for earthquake emergency medical service (EMS) systems. The framework integrates a three-stage stochastic programming model (Location–Assignment–Treatment, LAT) to address temporary hospital location, dynamic patient assignment, and treatment scheduling. To quantify interdependent damage among structural systems, architectural non-structural components, utilities, and medical equipment within permanent hospitals, Bayesian networks are employed for probabilistic modeling. Monte Carlo simulation is used to generate stochastic damage scenarios, and K-means++ clustering is applied to reduce dimensionality. Together, these techniques yield near-optimal EMS solutions with sub-1.0% gaps and minute-level runtimes, demonstrating robustness and scalability. Compared with a two-stage model, the proposed three-stage LAT framework further improves seismic resilience by 4.2%, highlighting the benefit of integrating temporary hospital location decisions. By explicitly accounting for structural damage, equipment failures, and dynamic patient assignment and treatment, this work advances stochastic programming methodologies for EMS resilience enhancement and provides actionable insights for post-disaster medical resource planning.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Evacuation network design and planning under traffic congestion: An application to wildfires in Canada
Authors: Alfredo Moreno, Valérie Bélanger, Marilène Cherkesly, Marie-Ève Rancourt
Abstract: Designing efficient evacuation networks is crucial for preparedness, as poorly planned and managed preventive evacuations can increase the time required for evacuees to reach safety zones or shelters, potentially resulting in adverse outcomes. While some studies have estimated traffic congestion, few have integrated multiple aspects of evacuation planning, within a unified framework. Yet, such integration is key to developing realistic and effective plans, despite the resulting complexity. In this study, we propose and solve a mixed-integer programming model to address the Evacuation Network Design and Planning Problem under Traffic Congestion (ENDPT). Our model jointly optimizes shelter locations, evacuation routes, and evacuee flows to minimize total evacuation time. Traffic congestion is captured using a formulation based on the Cell Transmission Model that incorporates time-varying road properties, multiple time periods, contraflow operations, and capacity constraints. To solve the ENDPT, we develop an exact method based on Benders decomposition and validate our approach through two complementary experiments. First, we generate instances from network topologies of communities that are threatened by wildfires to create standardized benchmarks. Results show that conventional models that ignore traffic dynamics can underestimate evacuation times by up to 60% compared to our integrated approach. Second, we develop a case study based on the 2023 wildfire evacuation of Chibougamau (Canada). This case study demonstrates the model’s practical value by generating tailored plans and assessing context-specific preparedness policies (e.g., showing that adding sheltering options with limited capacity can reduce traffic congestion by more than 95%) to support local decision-making.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Spatio-temporal weather and airspace graph network (SWAG-Net) for trajectory-based estimated time of arrival prediction
Authors: Ye Liu, Nana Chu, Kam K.H. Ng, Nuno Antunes Ribeiro, Changxin Zhu, Pak Wai Chan, Christy Y.Y. Leung
Abstract: Accurate prediction of flight estimated time of arrival (ETA) is crucial for efficient air traffic management (ATM) and operational planning. Several factors that affect arrival time, such as convective weather, traffic density and air traffic controllers’ instructions, pose significant challenges to ETA prediction due to their impact on airspace capacity and flight plans. This paper proposes a novel Spatio-temporal Weather and Airspace Graph Network (SWAG-Net) to predict flight ETA under various operational and meteorological scenarios. The proposed model integrates diverse data sources, including real-time multi-layer constant altitude plan position indicator (MCAPPI) weather radar, Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) and the geographical structure of the airspace’s arrival routes. By leveraging the dynamic adaptive spatio-temporal graph neural network, the model can capture both spatial and temporal dependencies, providing robust predictions in dynamic airspace and weather conditions. Experimental results demonstrate substantial enhancements in flight time estimation accuracy across diverse operational scenarios. It indicates a marked reduction in mean absolute error (MAE) to 1.28 min for a 30 min prediction horizon, representing a 41.6% improvement over traditional baseline models (MAE: 2.19 min). Meanwhile, the model indicates robust performance under challenging conditions, with pronounced accuracy gains observed in adverse weather and variable traffic density environments, and offers valuable insights into the impact of meteorological factors on flight operations. Further analysis shows that regional precipitation patterns within airspace greatly affect flight durations and the performance of predictive models. These findings suggest that the SWAG-Net framework has the potential to support weather-aware strategies for next-generation aviation systems.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Profitable pre-assigned pickup and delivery problem with product compatibility
Authors: Maryam Darvish, Simona Mancini
Abstract: This paper addresses a profitable pre-assigned pickup and delivery problem with product compatibility, motivated by a real case in less-than-truckload rural logistics. Couriers follow pre-assigned routes but may accept additional tasks if they are profitable and operationally feasible. Transported goods belong to different categories, some of which are mutually incompatible and must be handled sequentially or by different vehicles. A central decision maker assigns optional requests to available couriers, taking into account vehicle capacity, compatibility constraints, and detour-based compensation. The objective is to maximize platform revenue, defined as the total profit from served requests minus driver compensation. We propose a mixed-integer programming model to obtain optimal solutions for small-sized instances, and a multi-neighborhood matheuristic to extend analysis to larger scenarios. Computational experiments, including a real case study and sensitivity analyses, provide managerial insights into the trade-offs between profitability, detour costs, and product compatibility.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Non-fungible tokens as a bridge for integrated healthcare supply chains: an innovative approach focused on interoperability
Authors: Ghassan Al-Sumaidaee, Rami Alkhudary, Zeljko Zilic, Pierre Féniès, Srinivas Talluri
Abstract: This study tackles the ongoing challenge of interoperability within information systems, focusing on blockchain-enabled healthcare supply chains. We introduce a novel approach that uses non-fungible tokens (NFTs) to connect different blockchain systems. These NFTs serve as unique identifiers, allowing data integration while maintaining the confidentiality and decentralization of medical data. The model is validated through laboratory experiments and performance assessments. Throughput and latency are measured with results showing roughly 100 transactions per second and a latency of about 1.25 s. Scalability is evaluated by increasing system requests and transaction load. The system handles increased volume, but as it reaches high levels, such as 5000 transactions per second, response times slow considerably. Storage performance is tested with the InterPlanetary File System (IPFS), showing response times between 3 and 15 ms and a maximum throughput of 50.92 requests per second. Data embedding techniques are examined using SSIM and PSNR metrics, along with encryption and decryption durations, comparisons among LSB, DCT, and DWT algorithms, and assessment of data size impact. Smart contract efficiency is analyzed through deployment, minting, and updating processes, including confirmation times below one minute and gas usage analysis. The results support the ongoing discussion on blockchain interoperability in healthcare. The study also advocates a move toward a Selective Trust Architecture that shifts control from providers to users, relevant to metaverse technologies. Additionally, it offers valuable insights to practitioners working with decentralized healthcare supply chains.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: A two-echelon mobile charging system for electric vehicles with trucks and autonomous charging robots
Authors: Kechen Ouyang, Yitong Yu, Qingyun Tian, David Z.W. Wang
Abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) adoption is hindered by limited charging infrastructure and prolonged charging times. Mobile charging can alleviate these barriers by bringing charging services to parked vehicles. In practice, however, truck-based mobile chargers often struggle to access narrow residential streets and congested parking facilities, limiting their effectiveness in dense environments. To address this gap, this study proposes a novel two-echelon mobile charging system that combines trucks with autonomous charging robots (ACRs) to overcome accessibility limitations and improve operational efficiency. In this system, trucks transport ACRs between a central depot and satellite locations, while ACRs provide last-mile charging services within neighborhoods and parking facilities. We formulate this as a two-echelon mobile charger routing problem and develop a mixed-integer programming (MIP) model that captures routing decisions, time-window constraints, battery limitations, and ACR relocation requirements. Given the problem’s complexity, we develop a logic-based Benders decomposition approach combined with a branch-and-price algorithm, and introduce tailored problem-specific Benders cuts to accelerate convergence. Computational experiments demonstrate that our proposed algorithm efficiently solves the problem. Furthermore, our findings show that the coordinated truck-ACR operation significantly outperforms the standalone ACR-based approach.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Robust planning for bus fleet electrification and charging facility deployment
Authors: Yihan Gao, Wei Liu
Abstract: Electric buses are being increasingly adopted, given their significant environmental advantages. This paper examines the multi-period planning problem for bus fleet electrification and charging facility deployment within an urban bus service network. We first develop a deterministic model aimed at minimizing the sum of investment-related cost and emission-related cost. Subsequently, we depart from the assumption of deterministic bus service frequency and charging demand and account for their uncertainties, and adopt budget uncertainty sets that allow the flexibility to adjust the conservatism level of robust solutions. We then reformulate the robust optimization problem into a tractable mixed-integer linear programming model, which can be solved using existing solvers for smaller-scale problems. For large-scale instances, we design an exact solution approach that integrates Integer Benders decomposition and Lagrangian relaxation methods within a branch-and-cut framework. Compared to existing Integer Benders decomposition methods, our approach yields a tighter subproblem bound. Numerical results reveal an average bound improvement of 10.9%, which effectively reduces the frequency of exact subproblem evaluations by 77.0% on average across various planning horizons. Numerical studies on two Hong Kong bus systems indicate that our method outperforms both the Gurobi solver and heuristic algorithms. For large-scale instances where neither Gurobi nor heuristics can find an optimal solution, our approach consistently reaches optimality in at most 11.04 hours, demonstrating its computational efficiency and scalability for large-scale planning problems.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Routing and scheduling in home health care with time slot selection
Authors: Yanfeng Li, Xingdong Zhu, Zhaoyang Lu, Yu Jiang
Abstract: An increasing number of healthcare providers now offer patients the option of booking appointment time slots online. As patients’ preferences for time slots and caregivers vary with personal circumstances, determining which time slots to post online constitutes an emerging operational challenge. To address this issue, this study proposes to simultaneously optimize time slot selection and its subsequent dependent decisions, including healthcare providers’ routing and scheduling. The problem is formulated as a mixed-integer programming model, in which patients’ choice behavior is captured via a discrete choice model. The objective is to minimize caregivers’ routing costs and the expected penalty costs incurred when patients are not served within the designated time slots, while maximizing patient satisfaction, influenced by caregivers’ skill levels and patients’ familiarity with them. To solve the problem, a tailored Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS) algorithm, integrated with a time-slot perturbation mechanism and several newly designed operators, is developed. Numerical experiments are conducted on instances of varying scales, and the results demonstrate that the proposed ALNS algorithm significantly improves both solution quality and computational efficiency. Furthermore, sensitivity analyses on key model parameters including the number of the time slots selected to post online, utility coefficients and maximum skill level deviation reveal that certain parameters exert a particularly strong impact on the overall system performance. These findings provide theoretical foundations and practical implications for optimizing time slot selection to enhance the cost-efficiency of healthcare services.
Journal: Transportation Research Part E: Logistics and Transportation Review

Title: Methodological advances in online food delivery: A systematic review, taxonomy, and research outlook
Authors: Mohammadamin Tavasoli, Roberto Baldacci, Vahid Kayvanfar, Yu Zhang, Chefi Triki, Adel Elomri
